docs.title: tssa API Manual
docs.text:
tssa (Transportation Surrogate Safety Analysis) turns tracked road users from roadside video into ground trajectories, vehicle footprints and speeds for safety measures such as post-encroachment time (PET). It is the analysis side of dnt: dnt detects and tracks, and tssa works on the track files.

This site is generated with MkDocs and mkdocstrings from the Python source in src/tssa.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install -e .                 # the package
pip install -e ".[detect]"       # plus the detectors used by tssa.footprint.detect (torch, ultralytics, OpenCV)
pip install -e ".[docs]"         # plus the tools that build this manual

Python 3.9 or newer. OpenCV is needed only to fit a homography, run the detectors or rasterise masks. Loading a saved homography and projecting with it use NumPy only.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package What it does Main entry point tssa.footprint Vehicle ground footprints (reference point, oriented polygon, speed) from tracked boxes, with seven methods M1-M7 VehFootPrinter tssa.smooth Segment ground tracks at jumps, fill gaps and smooth positions TrackSmoother tssa.speed Velocity and speed from smoothed positions SpeedCalculator tssa.transform Image to ground homographies, lens distortion, pinhole camera fit DistortedHomography, GroundModel tssa.engine Point, line and zone geometry for track matching functions tssa.core Earlier analyses: counts, lanes, speed meters, interactions, near misses, yielding Count, LaneDetector, ... tssa.annotation, tssa.io Drawing results on video, reading track files Annotation, read_track

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
track file (pixels)
  -> tssa.transform     image <-> world (m) homography, with lens distortion
  -> tssa.footprint     reference point per row (M1-M7, per-class fallback chain) + 2 x 2 covariance
  -> tssa.smooth        segment, fill gaps, RTS smoothing
  -> tssa.speed         velocity and speed (mph)
  -> tssa.footprint     oriented polygon per row -> GeoDataFrame for PET

VehFootPrinter.estimate() runs the last four steps in one call. See the Quickstart.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
• Positions are in the homography's world metres (for example UTM).
  • Vehicle sizes and distance settings of FootprintConfig are in feet.
  • Speeds are in mph unless you pass a metric SpeedCalculator.

docs.title: tssa.footprint: vehicle ground footprint from tracked boxes (VehFootPrinter)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-11-10 Status: approved by the user, 2026-11-10 (rev 4.1); rev 4.2 is an implementation note (§4.3). §19 adds the validation results (2026-11-11). Q6 and Q7 answered the same day (§16); nothing is open. - rev 4.1: addresses review_2026-11-10-213328.md (response); §15 summary of invalid-projection rows only (editorial). - rev 4: addresses review_2026-11-10-211138.md (response): - M7 admission is separate from the box-projection gate, with three row kinds (§7.7, §7.10, §9); - the width-hold inequality now matches the study code (§7.6); - one precedence rule for admission in compare() (§7.8, §11.2); - the UTM round-trip test is split into an internal and a public tolerance (§14.2). - rev 3: addresses review_2026-11-10-205948.md (response): - invalid projections are kept on the grid, never measured (§5.2, §9); - a complete segmented-input contract for the smoother (§5.2); - measurement admission follows finite positions, not interp, and supplied covariances are final (§5.1, §5.2, §7.9); - rts_smooth gets a guard and the correct start time (§5.3), and orientation handles zero or one native rows (§10.2); - native axes are kept on vehicles that never move, with a front_known flag (§10.2); - OpenCV-free loading and projection, including the existing homography module (§2, §8, §13); - an explicit ground-model adapter with image size (§4.2); - unit-aware heading threshold (§10.1); - native-only compare() disables admission, and keeps every row (§11.2); - detector row selection is independent of the config (§6.4); - a study snapshot before porting (§17, phase 0). - rev 2: the user's answers to rev 1's open questions (2026-11-10): - Q1: the class is VehFootPrinter. - Q2: sizes and distance settings are in feet. - Q3: port M1–M7 together, not only the recommended subset. - Q4: "your suggestion": take the 2 × 2 covariance path, which needs two backward-compatible additions to tssa.smooth (§5). - Q5: tssa provides the detectors (keypoints, cuboids, SAM masks) and the detection-to-track matching (§6), as an optional install. - rev 1: first draft (M1, M2, M3, M6 only; detectors and covariance left open).

Source study: D:\apps\miami-win\test\speed (NW afternoon clip, A1A Collins Ave & 17th St), referred to below as the study. Its documents are the algorithm specification for every method; this design says how each one becomes part of tssa, and what changes on the way. - docs/2026-11-05-vehicle-footprint-design.md (rev 5.1), the base design: M1–M6, camera, smoothing, orientation. - docs/2026-11-06-vehicle-footprint-run-report.md, the run report: results, recommendation, large-vehicle changes, rulings R0–R23. - docs/2026-11-08-m7-wheel-anchored-design.md (rev 7), the M7 design, and docs/2026-11-08-m7-build-notes.md, the M7 notes: decisions made while building M7 (up to "Round limit 20 -> 30", 2026-11-10).

Target package: tssa 0.0.2.4. New subpackage src/tssa/footprint/, new src/tssa/transform/camera.py and ground.py, additions to src/tssa/smooth/, and lazy OpenCV in src/tssa/transform/homography.py.

docs.title: 1. Intent
docs.text:
The study compared seven ways to get a vehicle's ground position and footprint from a DNT bbox, through one shared segmentation and smoother. This design moves all seven into tssa, so a later project (PET, conflicts, speed) can get vehicle footprints from tracked boxes and video without the study's scripts, and can still compare methods.

tssa already has the steps around it: - tssa.transform.DistortedHomography: image ↔ ground; - tssa.smooth.TrackSmoother: segments and smooths ground positions; - tssa.speed.SpeedCalculator: speed from smoothed positions.

None of them knows where on the vehicle its input point is. Today a user projects the bbox bottom-centre (the study's M1) and smooths that. The study showed this point is the worst choice for PET: it sits 4.5 ft from the consensus of the independent cues, its bias depends on direction (left turns +3.8 ft ahead), it shifts PET by up to 0.43 s (p90; 0.75 s on right turns), and it reads trap speeds 0.9 mph lower than M6.

VehFootPrinter supplies the missing step: video + pixel boxes → a ground reference point at the body centre, with its covariance (before smoothing) → an oriented polygon of the right size (after smoothing).

docs.title: 1.1 The seven methods
docs.text:
Name Study method Needs Native output Study result M1 bbox bottom-centre homography point (foot of the box, not the body centre) 4.59 ft from M6; PET shift p90 0.43 s M2 M1 moved half a nominal width away from the camera homography point 1.65 ft from M6; |Δ speed| 0.40 mph; no inference M3 nominal rectangle at the reference heading, fitted to the bbox homography, ψ_ref rectangle, orientation imposed trucks 1.4 ft from M6 (M2: 6.7 ft) M4 CarFusion wheel keypoints keypoints, camera, ψ_ref point + directed heading 6.1% coverage; 1.18 ft from M6 M5 SAM lower outline, nominal rectangle fit masks rectangle + axis 58.7% coverage; e2e jitter doubles M6 UrbanOmniDetect-2 cuboid bottom face cuboids measured quadrilateral + axis 99.5% coverage; recommended for PET and speed M7 wheel-anchored rigid-body fit per segment (buses, trucks) masks, camera, M2, ψ_ref centre + directed heading + fitted L, W, covariance 19 of 25 display solves pass (run 20261110_161113_s0); the user reviewed the M7 clips on 2026-11-10

The default chains (§7.8) follow the study's recommendation (M6 for cars) and its combined PET product (M7 for buses and trucks, M6 next, then the class fallback).

docs.title: 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
docs.text:
Goals - One public class, VehFootPrinter, with a frozen FootprintConfig, in the style of TrackSmoother / SmoothConfig. - All seven methods as registered locators (§7), usable alone, in per-class fallback chains, or side by side (compare()). - Per row: reference point, 2 × 2 position covariance, the locator that supplied it, why the others failed, native orientation and size. - After smoothing, per row: footprint orientation, motion heading, length and width in feet with their source, four corners; optionally shapely polygons. - Detector wrappers and matching (§6), so tssa can go from video to footprints. - A pinhole camera fitted to a ground homography (§8), needed by M4 and M7. - The study's synthetic tests ported under tests/, and one validation run that reproduces the study's NW-clip results (§14).

Non-goals (this round) - The study's evaluation machinery: the three products (metric-native, metric end-to-end, display), eligibility and analysis-zone rules for metrics, plausibility table, stop mask, review clips, pinned-input hashing, sample-independence checks, camera-sensitivity reports. compare() gives a project what it needs to build its own. - M7's metric solves per eligible run. tssa has one product, so M7 solves once per segment, the study's display solve. - Manual footprint keyframes (the user decided not to annotate, 2026-11-08). - Training models, shipping weights, real-time processing, PET itself.

Anti-goals (failure even if it "works") - A method looks better because it was smoothed differently. Every locator goes through the same segmentation and smoother, with the same noise model (§7.9). The only exception is M7's admitted pseudo-measurements, which carry M7's own covariance and are marked (§7.7). - Imposed sizes reported as measured. dims_source says whether a size was measured, partly prior, or nominal (M7: by information, M7 design §8.3). - Silent drops or invented support. Every input row comes back once. A row without a reference point says which locators were tried and why each failed. An M7 row with no observation of its own is never native. - Heavy imports for light use. Without torch, ultralytics or OpenCV installed, these must work: import tssa; loading a saved HomographyTransform or DistortedHomography (load_json, load_matrix) and projecting with it; fitting the pinhole camera; and M1, M2, M3, M4 and M6. OpenCV is still needed to fit a new homography, and for M5 and M7, which rasterise mask contours. torch and ultralytics load only when a detector runs (§6, §8, §13). - Study constants or machine paths in the code. NW-clip values are defaults with a cited source; checkpoints and repository paths are arguments. - Silent drift from the study. Every deliberate change is listed in §15.

docs.title: 3. Where it sits in the pipeline
docs.text:
video ─► detect.run(...)            keypoints, cuboids, masks    (optional; §6; or bring your own tables)
                 │
tracks ──────────┼─► VehFootPrinter.locate()
                 │      1. project M1, build ONE segment grid  (TrackSmoother.segment, §5.2, §9)
                 │      2. M2 everywhere, reference pass: smooth M2 → ψ_ref        (§9)
                 │      3. per class, run its chain of locators on the grid        (§7)
                 │         → seg, fp_x, fp_y, fp_cov_*, fp_source, native orientation and size
                 ▼
            TrackSmoother.smooth(segmented=True)  same grid, covariance columns  (§5)
                 ▼
            SpeedCalculator.calculate()
                 ▼
            VehFootPrinter.polygons()  orientation, size, corners               (§10)

estimate() runs locate → smooth → speed → polygons with vehicle defaults (§11.3). locate() and polygons() stay public for users who want their own smoother or speed settings. compare() runs several methods on the same grid (§11.2).

The order follows base design §8.1: segmentation is built once, before any method; reference points are fixed before smoothing; orientation and polygon come after, from the smoothed motion.

docs.title: 4.1 Tracks
docs.text:
A DataFrame, one row per (track, frame); column names configurable (§12):

Column Meaning frame integer frame number, zero-based, the video's frame index track track id x, y, w, h bbox top-left and size in distorted image pixels cls class id per row (DNT: 2 car, 5 bus, 7 truck). The class used is the track's majority class, cls_track. interp (optional) 0 detected, 1 filled upstream

All tracks of a frame should be passed, including tracks the user does not want footprints for. M7 drops outline columns that a nearer box covers, and detector matching is one-to-one over every box of a frame (run report R21). locate(..., only_tracks=[...]) limits the output without hiding the other boxes.

docs.title: 4.2 Homography and the ground-model adapter
docs.text:
VehFootPrinter wraps whatever it is given in tssa.transform.ground.GroundModel (new):

GroundModel.wrap(homography, image_size=None) -> GroundModel
    image_to_world(uv) / world_to_image(EN)   # distorted pixels <-> world metres
    undistort(uv) / distort(uv_u)             # identity when the homography has no distortion model
    world_to_undistorted(EN)                  # direct through the inner undistorted-image homography when there is one
    image_size                                # (width, height) px
  • Distortion.
  • For DistortedHomography, undistort and distort are its own, and world_to_undistorted uses its inner homography directly. The round trip through distort() would add the iteration error of its 20-step inverse.
  • For HomographyTransform, or any object with only image_to_world / world_to_image, both are the identity and world_to_undistorted = world_to_image.
  • An object that has one of undistort / distort but not the other is rejected.
  • Image size. Taken from the explicit image_size argument (VehFootPrinter(..., image_size=(640, 480))), else from the homography's image_size attribute (DistortedHomography has one). If the two disagree, ValueError. If neither exists, construction fails with ValueError: the edge flag (§7.10) and the camera's principal-point prior (§8) both need it.
  • Pixel spaces. The camera works only in undistorted pixels. Its fit targets are world_to_undistorted of the zone grid, and its consistency check compares distort(camera.project(X, z = 0)) with world_to_image(X), as base design §5 specifies. M4 hub points and M7 tyre candidates are undistorted before they meet the camera (M7 design §5).

docs.title: 4.3 Detection tables
docs.text:
Written by tssa.footprint.detect (§6), or by the user's own pipeline in the same format. All pixels are distorted image pixels, keyed by (track, frame) after matching.

Table Columns Used by keypoints track, frame, iou, u0, v0 … u3, v3 (CarFusion wheels 0 RF, 1 LF, 2 RB, 3 LB) M4, M7 (optional cue) cuboids track, frame, iou, gu0, gv0 … gu3, gv3 (bottom-face corners, any start, any winding) M6 masks MaskTable: (track, frame) → list of contour polygons (k, 2) of every mask component, largest first, plus .outlines: the lower outline taken from the raw mask at segmentation time M5 (the stored outline, else one rebuilt from the contours), M7 (components with at least 5% of the area)

One SAM pass serves both M5 and M7 (the study ran SAM twice, §15): - M5 reads the lower outline that MaskSegmenter takes from the raw mask, exactly the study's M5 input. Without one (masks from elsewhere), it rebuilds the outline from the contours. - M7 keeps the components holding at least M7_MIN_COMPONENT_FRAC (5%) of the summed area + perimeter, the rule the study applied when it wrote its SAM cache. Applied to an already filtered table it keeps every component, so the study's cache works as is.

rev 4.2 (implementation, 2026-11-10): rev 4.1 stored only the 5% components and rebuilt M5's outline from them. The validation run measured the cost: outlines identical to the study's on 3,769 of 4,129 bus and truck rows, and M5 validity changed on 62 of them (§19).

docs.title: 4.4 Camera zone
docs.text: M4 and M7 need the pinhole camera of §8, which is fitted over a ground region. zone: a shapely polygon in world metres. Helper: zone_from_points(world_points, buffer_ft=15) (base design §7: GCP convex hull + 15 ft). Without a zone, camera-dependent locators fail with camera_invalid.

docs.title: 5. Changes to tssa.smooth (the answer to Q4)
docs.text:
Recommendation. Use the study's full measurement covariance, not a scalar σ. Two reasons: - The ground scale of a pixel is strongly directional in this view: the largest-to-smallest ratio has median 3.3 and p95 5.0 (base design §9). A scalar σ under-smooths along the camera ray and over-smooths across it. - M7's display pseudo-measurements carry their own 2 × 2 covariance (M7 design §9.3). A per-row covariance column carries them with no special path, replacing the study's R_override.

All additions below are backward compatible: calls that use none of the new arguments give identical results, and the existing smooth and speed tests must pass unchanged.

docs.title: 5.1 Per-row covariance
docs.text: SmoothConfig.cov_cols: tuple[str, str, str] | None = None: names of per-row covariance columns (xx, xy, yy) in m². Three columns make R symmetric by construction. - The rts kind uses them as the measurement covariance R on measured rows where all three are finite; otherwise sigma_col; otherwise the method's sigma. - A supplied covariance is final. fill_scale is applied only to noise that comes from sigma_col or the method's sigma, never to cov_cols. Whoever writes the covariance applies any inflation. For VehFootPrinter that rule is §7.9. - A measured row whose covariance is not positive definite (xx > 0, yy > 0, xx·yy − xy² > 0) raises ValueError. - Kinds without a noise model (ma, sg) ignore it, as they ignore sigma_col today.

docs.title: 5.2 Segmenting once, smoothing many times
docs.text:
TrackSmoother.segment(tracks, ref_tracks=None, allow_missing=False) -> DataFrame

The public form of today's _grid. It returns the structural table only: track, frame, seg, seg_len, interp, fill_reason, gap_id, one row per input row plus the inserted rows (interp = 2). No positions are returned, so none can be reused by mistake.

With allow_missing=True, rows with a non-finite position are accepted and kept: - Jump detection and gap classification use only the finite rows. A run of missing rows between two finite rows counts as part of the gap between them. - Interior run, gap filled (short enough, plausible implied speed, no jump): the missing rows stay in the segment with their own interp (0 or 1) and fill_reason = "no_position". Frames with no row at all are inserted as today (interp = 2). - Interior run, gap not filled: the track is split there, and the missing rows get seg = −1, fill_reason = "no_position". - Prefix, suffix, or whole track (missing rows before a track's first finite row, after its last, or on a track with no finite row): seg = −1, fill_reason = "no_position". They are never extrapolated.

Without allow_missing, a non-finite position raises, as today.

TrackSmoother.smooth(tracks, ref_tracks=None, segmented=False)

With segmented=True, the input already carries the structural columns seg, interp, fill_reason (from segment() or from VehFootPrinter.locate()). Then: - No re-segmentation. The input is validated: no repeated (track, frame), and every (track, seg ≥ 0) has consecutive frames; otherwise ValueError. seg_len is recomputed. seg, interp and fill_reason are input columns in this mode, so they pass through unchanged and are not clashes. The smoother adds only <pos>_smooth and fallback (or the compare() columns). - Measurement admission follows the positions, not interp. A row is a measurement exactly when it has seg ≥ 0 and both position values are finite. interp is provenance only. It selects fill_scale for σ-based noise on interp = 1 rows, and it no longer clears observations. A finite position on an interp = 2 row (an M7 pseudo-measurement on an inserted frame, §7.7) is measured. - Nothing from the segmentation pass is reused. Observations come only from this call's position columns. Kinds that need a value on every row (ma, sg, and the short-segment fallback) get this call's measurements linearly interpolated across unmeasured rows of the segment, and held constant before the first and after the last measurement. - Coordinates. The local origin is computed from this call's finite positions (floor of the minimum, as today), and the output is returned in input coordinates, rounded to three decimals like every added numeric column today. - Segments without enough measurements: - 0 measured rows: NaN positions, fallback = 1; - 1 measured row: that position on that row, NaN elsewhere, fallback = 1; - fewer than the method's minimum otherwise: the interpolated raw positions, fallback = 1, as today. - seg = −1 rows are returned with NaN positions and fallback = 1.

Without segmented, behaviour is unchanged.

This is how one segmentation serves every method, as the study required (base design §7, anti-goal 1), without any method seeing another's positions.

docs.title: 5.3 rts_smooth fixes
docs.text: tssa.smooth.methods.rts_smooth needs two fixes, both found by the review: - Guard. Fewer than 2 measured rows raises ValueError with a clear message, not IndexError. Every caller checks first (§5.2, §10.2). - Start time. The forward pass starts at the first measured row i0, from the state of rows i0, i1 as today. Rows before i0 take the smoothed state at i0, extrapolated backward at its constant velocity: x_k = x̂_{i0} − (i0 − k)·dt·v̂_{i0}. Today the filter starts at row 0 with the state of row i0. On exact constant-velocity data with a 10-frame missing prefix, that gives 1.54 m at frame 0 where the truth is 0. - Existing callers are unaffected: today every segment starts with a measured row (inserted rows lie only between observations), so i0 = 0.

docs.title: 6.1 Packaging
docs.text:
• Extra: pip install tssa[detect] adds torch, ultralytics, opencv-python, huggingface_hub. requirements.txt already lists OpenCV.
  • Every import of these is lazy, inside the function that needs it. A missing package raises ImportError naming the extra.
  • UrbanOmniDetect-2 is not pip-installable. CuboidDetector(weights, repo_root) puts repo_root first on sys.path and imports v2.hybrid_v2 before loading, as the study's infer.load_uod does.
  • No weights ship with tssa. The keypoint model downloads from Hugging Face at a pinned revision (default: the study's 48b5795f3b79cdfe7ff6588812aa388a6a7fdd9d of kiselyovd/vehicle-keypoints, weights.pt). An unpinned revision raises.

docs.title: 6.2 Classes
docs.text:
Class Model Output table Study defaults KeypointDetector(repo, filename, revision, conf=0.08, imgsz=640) CarFusion YOLO pose keypoints infer.run_keypoints CuboidDetector(weights, repo_root, conf=0.08, imgsz=640, prefer_cls=(2, 5, 7)) UrbanOmniDetect-2 cuboids infer.run_uod MaskSegmenter(weights, min_component_frac=0.0) SAM2.1, box-prompted with each track bbox masks infer.run_sam_full

Full-frame inference for keypoints and cuboids; SAM is prompted with the requested rows' boxes (all of a frame in one call). Masks are > 0.5, resized to the frame if needed, and stored as external contours (CHAIN_APPROX_NONE) of every component (by default), largest first, together with the row's lower outline from the raw mask.

docs.title: 6.3 Matching
docs.text: match_frame(track_xyxy, det_xyxy, min_iou=0.3, det_cls=None, prefer=None): one-to-one assignment of detections to every track box of the frame, maximising total IoU (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment), edges below min_iou removed, preferred classes first (run report R21). It needs only numpy and scipy, so it lives in the core package (footprint/match.py) for users with their own detectors.

docs.title: 6.4 Runner and cache
docs.text:
tables = detect.run(video, tracks, detectors=[KeypointDetector(), CuboidDetector(w, root), MaskSegmenter(w)],
                    rows=None, cache_dir=None)          # -> {"keypoints": df, "cuboids": df, "masks": MaskTable}
- Frames are read once, sequentially (cv2.VideoCapture), and every detector runs on each frame read. - Two separate inputs. - tracks is the matching context: every box of every frame. It is always used whole, for the one-to-one matching of §6.3, however few rows are requested. - rows selects the output (and cached) rows. - rows default, independent of any configuration: every row of tracks, for every detector. The runner knows nothing about chains. - To infer only what a configuration needs, ask the printer: vfp.required_rows(tracks) -> {"keypoints": df, "cuboids": df, "masks": df}. It returns, per table, the rows of tracks whose class chain contains a locator that needs that table (a custom car chain with M5 makes car rows appear under masks). Pass the result as rows=, either as one dict or per detector. - Cache (base design §10), optional: cache_dir/<detector>/<key>/, where key hashes the video file, the full track table (the matching context), the weights (file SHA-256 or HF revision), the detector parameters and a per-detector CODE_VERSION. A changed setting gives a new key, never silent reuse. A run infers only rows the cache lacks, and saves every 200 frames. MaskTable is stored as npz. The study's lesson applies: arrays are read once per load, not per row (run report, "Performance fix").

docs.title: 7.1 Contract
docs.text:
@register_locator("M5", needs=("masks",), scope="row", point_only=False)
def locate_m5(rows: pd.DataFrame, ctx: LocateContext) -> LocatorResult: ...
- scope="row": the locator sees any subset of rows. scope="segment" (M7): it sees whole segments of the grid, consecutive frames including filled ones. - ctx: the homography, the camera (or None), the config, the grid with cls_track, ref_heading_deg and the M2 points, and the detection tables by name. - LocatorResult, arrays aligned to rows: - ok, fail_reason; - x, y (world m); - optional cov (n, 2, 2): only M7 supplies one; the others get the shared model of §7.9; - orient_deg, orient_kind (axis / directed / none); - len_ft, wid_ft (measured size, or NaN); - support (native / kinematic); - an extras dict of diagnostic columns, namespaced by the method (m4_*, m5_*, m7_*). - A locator whose needs are not supplied fails every row with not_supplied.

Algorithms are ported from the study's code, not rewritten. §7.2–7.7 name the source and say only what changes.

docs.title: 7.2 M1, M2, M3
docs.text: Ported from geometry.m1_points, geometry.m2_points and m3.solve_m3 (base design §6): - M1 is point_only: polygons() gives it no corners. - M2: away = unit(world(u, v − 1) − world(u, v)) at the bbox bottom-centre; moved W_nom / 2 along it. - M3: solve the centre so the nominal rectangle at ψ_ref has its lowest projected corner on the bbox bottom and its projected horizontal midpoint at the bbox centre. LM from the M2 point; valid below 0.5 px. Fail reasons no_heading, no_solution. The orientation is ψ_ref, imposed.

docs.title: 7.3 M4 (wheel keypoints)
docs.text:
Ported from m4.solve_m4 and m4.front_conflict (base design §6.1). Unchanged, including: - the four label permutations; - the interior side from the other pair or from camera-away, never from the labels; - the hub-to-contact drop, because the landmark is the hub (run report: confirmed on crops; wheel_landmark = "hub" in the config); - the per-track front_conflict flag.

Fail reasons: no_match, no_valid_pair, side_ambiguous, camera_invalid, no_heading. Extras: m4_pair_side, m4_label_case, m4_interior_source, m4_side_reject, m4_front_flipped, m4_wheelbase_ft, m4_track_ft, m4_front_conflict.

docs.title: 7.4 M5 (SAM outline)
docs.text:
Ported from m5.native_m5: - lower outline from the mask contours; - R23: drop points more than 1 px below the bbox bottom; - fit a nominal-size rectangle from fixed starts at 0/45/90/135° (R19); - R20: mirror the fit away from the camera.

Fail reasons: no_match, few_columns (< 8), fit_residual (> m5_max_resid_ft, 1.0 ft, untuned in the study). Extras: m5_cols, m5_resid_ft, m5_sides, m5_flipped.

docs.title: 7.5 M6 (cuboid)
docs.text:
Ported from m6.native_m6 and face_geometry: - project the four corners; - opposite-edge means give length and width; - doubled-angle mean of the long edges gives the axis; - the corner mean is the reference point.

Fail reasons: no_match (no row, IoU < 0.3, non-finite), implausible_size (length or width under m6_size_gate = 0.5 of nominal; run report "Large-vehicle handling"). The raw projected corners are kept as m6_raw_c1x … m6_raw_c4y, with m6_len_ft, m6_wid_ft, m6_iou.

docs.title: 7.6 M7 (wheel-anchored rigid fit), scope="segment"
docs.text:
Ported from m7.py, m7_candidates.py, and the job and table parts of m7_runner.py, in the state of 2026-11-10 (run 20261110_161113_s0). This is the M7 design rev 7 plus the M7 notes' later decisions: - front rule travel (2026-11-09); - width held at the class prior when the silhouette resolves width coarser than the threshold (2026-11-10). The study code is authoritative (m7.py: w_held = M7_W_HOLD_FT_PER_PX is not None and w_ft_per_px > M7_W_HOLD_FT_PER_PX): - w_ft_per_px is the width change per pixel of far-end silhouette, median over frames (width_resolution). Larger means coarser. - Held when w_ft_per_px > 0.3, a strict inequality: exactly 0.3 is not held. - w_ft_per_px = inf (no frame's extreme column moves with W) is held. - w_hold_ft_per_px = None never holds. - a width on its bound does not fail the solve (M7_W_BOUND_FAILS = False); - fitted tyre inset; - tyre lowest-point model; - image-edge σ; - pair-wheelbase restarts; - 30 outer rounds; - tandem and far-side targets off.

All M7_* settings move into FootprintConfig.m7 (§12.2) with these values.

Per segment of a cls 5/7 track (m7_classes): 1. Frozen observations: frame_obs_from_mask on every row with a mask. Other boxes of the same frame come from the full track table (§4.1). 2. Initial pose (study m7_runner._init_pose, then m7.initial_x): - centre: the M2 points (§9), linearly interpolated across rows without one; - heading: ψ_ref interpolated as a unit vector, or the path direction where ψ_ref is missing. 3. Fit: solve_track. Segments shorter than min_support_frames (10) fail with too_few_frames. 4. Rows: - wheels2 / wheel_front / wheel_rear / silhouette rows are native; - kinematic rows are ok = False, fail_reason = no_observation, and their pose is kept in m7_x, m7_y, m7_psi_deg; - a failed solve fails every row with its gate reason (param_bound, wheel_resid, articulated_suspect, …).

Runtime. - The study's 49 solves took 46 min wall on 12 workers; one 592-frame truck segment alone took 45 min. - VehFootPrinter(..., workers=N) solves segments in a process pool (one BLAS thread each). - cache_dir stores each solve under a key that hashes its observations, initial pose, camera, the m7 settings and the solver's code version (study m7_runner.job_key).

Extras: the M7 design §9.4 columns with the m7_ prefix (support, own pose, per-solve parameters, size sources, uncertainty, flags), plus m7_w_held.

docs.title: 7.7 M7 pseudo-measurements
docs.text:
M7 design §9.3, user decision Q2, adapted to the one-product world. - Admission (the study's predicate, products._product): a row becomes a measurement when - its segment's M7 solve passed, - m7_support = kinematic, and - its M7 pose and m7_cov_centre are finite.

Nothing about the box is checked. Admission does not look at the projection gate (§7.10), the box fields or the Jacobian, so it applies to all three row kinds of §7.10 that lie in a segment (seg ≥ 0): - inserted frames (interp = 2): no box at all; - original rows whose projection was rejected: inside a segment, fill_reason = "no_position". Admission overrides the rejection, as in the study, where the display gate was proj_valid and admission ignored it. The M7 pose comes from the camera and motion model, not from the bbox bottom. - original rows with a valid projection.

Never admitted: rows with seg = −1, which belong to no segment and no solve. The smoother measures any segment row with a finite position (§5.2), so an admitted point is used, not cleared. - No box-derived values on admitted rows. Their fp_x, fp_y is the M7 pose and their covariance is the one below. fp_sigma is computed from it; no box, Jacobian or fill_meas_scale enters. - Native M7 rows are gated like any box row, also as in the study (nat_ok = native_valid & gate): a wheels2 / wheel_* / silhouette row whose projection was rejected is not used as a native measurement. It is not admitted either, because admission requires kinematic support, so the next locator in the chain tries it. - Covariance: R = kin_meas_scale² · m7_cov_centre + (kin_sd_floor_ft · 0.3048)² · I (defaults 2.0 and 0.5 ft). It is final (§5.1), so no interp-based inflation is added, whatever the row's interp. - Marking: fp_source = "M7", fp_support = "kinematic". - Precedence: M7 native rows, then admitted rows, then the next locator in the chain. - admit_kinematic=False turns it off, giving the study's metric behaviour (no pseudo-measurements).

docs.title: 7.8 Chains
docs.text:
Each class has an ordered chain. The first locator that succeeds on a row supplies its reference point. Defaults:

cls_track Default chain Source 2 car M6 → M2 run report recommendation 5 bus M7 → M6 → M2 M7 design §9.3 and §9.6 7 truck M7 → M6 → M3 → M2 same; FALLBACK_BY_CLASS = {7: "M3"}; the final M2 catches rows with no heading other M2, with default_size_ft my call
  • Locators whose tables were not supplied fail with not_supplied, so without detections the chains reduce to M2 / M3 → M2.
  • M4 and M5 are in no default chain (the study rejected them for production). Users add them through chains.
  • Aliases (added in 0.0.2.12, Q7 in §16): bottom_centre M1, nominal_shift M2, nominal_box M3, wheel_keypoints M4, sam_outline M5, cuboid M6, wheel_fit M7. Chains and compare() accept either name; the printer resolves aliases when it is built, so results (fp_source, fp_fail, method) always carry the M name. register_locator(..., aliases=...) and register_alias() add names for user locators.
  • A chain of one locator has no fallback: failed rows have no measurement, and the smoother predicts them. For M7 this is the study's native-only product only with admit_kinematic=False; with admission on (the default), kinematic rows are still measured. compare(fallback=None) turns admission off for you (§11.2).
  • Mixing sources inside a track adds jumps, because the locators disagree by 1–2 ft (cars: M2 vs M6 1.6 ft). fp_source records it per row.

docs.title: 7.9 Shared noise model
docs.text:
For every locator except M7's admitted rows, the measurement covariance is the study's (smoothlib.methods.measurement_cov): 

R = (sigma_k · h)² · J Jᵀ      J = 1-px Jacobian of image_to_world at the bbox bottom-centre, h = box height
sigma_k = 0.03 (study RTS_SIGMA_K). It comes from the box, not from the locator, so no locator looks steadier because it was given a smaller σ. It is written as fp_cov_xx, fp_cov_xy, fp_cov_yy, plus fp_sigma = sqrt(trace(R) / 2) for smoothers that take a scalar.

Scaling by support type. Supplied covariances are final (§5.1), so locate() applies every inflation itself:

Row Covariance box-based locator (M1–M7 native) on an original row with a valid projection, interp = 0 R as above box-based locator, interp = 1 (box filled upstream) fill_meas_scale² · R, fill_meas_scale = 4.0 (study FILL_MEAS_SCALE, applied as in the study's smooth_series) M7 admitted pseudo-measurement, any interp §7.7, no further scaling no reference point NaN; the row is not measured

fp_sigma is computed from the scaled R. A smoother given sigma_col="fp_sigma" instead of the covariance columns would apply its own fill_scale on top, so estimate() always passes the covariance columns (§11.3).

docs.title: 7.10 Shared per-row checks
docs.text:
• Three row kinds. fp_row_kind tells them apart; fp_proj_valid is the gate result (False on inserted rows, as the study's proj_valid):
fp_row_kind Row Box observation M7 admission (§7.7) box original row, projection valid yes: every locator may run if kinematic box_rejected original row, projection rejected no: every native locator fails it with projection if seg ≥ 0 and kinematic inserted frame inserted into a gap (interp = 2), no box no: row-scope locators are not run, fp_fail = "no_box". M7's segment solve spans the frame but has no observation there, so the frame is kinematic. if kinematic
  • Projection gate (base design §7), on original rows only: the bottom-centre projection is invalid when non-finite, when the local scale (largest singular value of J) exceeds max_ft_per_px (2.0), or, if a zone is given, when it is outside the zone buffered by gate_buffer_ft (100). The gate governs box observations (every locator's native result). It does not govern M7 admission.
  • Image edge: fp_edge = True when the bbox is within edge_px (2) of an image border. A flag only.

docs.title: 7.11 locate() output
docs.text:
Input columns first, unchanged; the grid's inserted rows are added (interp = 2). Every input row is present exactly once, including rows with an invalid projection (seg = −1 or fill_reason = "no_position", §9) and rows of tracks outside only_tracks (which keep their structural columns but get no fp_* values). Then:

Column Meaning cls_track, seg, fill_reason, gap_id class and the shared grid (§5.2). The input's interp is updated in place, as TrackSmoother does. fp_x, fp_y reference point (world m); NaN when no locator succeeded fp_cov_xx, fp_cov_xy, fp_cov_yy, fp_sigma §7.9 / §7.7 fp_source supplying locator, or none fp_support native, kinematic (M7 admitted) or empty fp_fail failures before it, ;-joined, e.g. M7:param_bound;M6:implausible_size fp_orient_deg, fp_orient_kind native orientation of the supplying locator fp_len_ft, fp_wid_ft measured size of the supplying locator (M6, M7), else NaN fp_row_kind, fp_proj_valid box / box_rejected / inserted, and the gate result (§7.10) fp_edge, ref_heading_deg §7.10, §9 m4_*, m5_*, m6_*, m7_* extras of every locator that ran on the row

docs.title: 8. Pinhole camera (tssa.transform.camera)
docs.text:
Ported from the study's camera.py (base design §5). It is a transform, so it goes into tssa.transform next to the homography. - PinholeCamera: project(XYZ) (world 3-D → undistorted px) and ray(uv). - PinholeCamera.fit(homography, zone, f_fixed=None, free_principal=True, pp_prior=1e-3): least-squares fit of f, (cx, cy), R and C to a 1 m grid over the zone, mapped with the homography. A weak prior pulls (cx, cy) toward the image centre, which picks one exact camera out of the family (R18). - consistency(cam, homography, zone): RMS and max ground-projection residual; ok at RMS ≤ 1 px and max ≤ 3 px. - sensitivity(...): refits at f × 0.87 / 1.0 / 1.13. - hub_to_contact(cam, uv, r_m): the ray meets z = r, then drops vertically.

  • Pixel space and image size come from the GroundModel adapter (§4.2):
  • fit targets: world_to_undistorted of the zone grid;
  • consistency check: distort(project(X, z = 0)) against world_to_image(X);
  • principal-point prior: toward the centre of image_size.

fit takes a GroundModel; a plain homography is wrapped, and fails without an image size. - No OpenCV. - cv2.Rodrigues becomes scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.from_rotvec / as_rotvec. - The initial plane homography (cv2.findHomography(…, 0), plain least squares) becomes a normalised DLT in numpy. - The ported test_camera checks parity, and so does the NW-clip camera of §14.3 (f = 319.55 px, (cx, cy) = (334.10, 240.13), height 6.73 m, within 0.01 px / 0.001 m).

VehFootPrinter fits the camera lazily, the first time a locator needs it. A failed consistency check makes M4 and M7 fail with camera_invalid (base design §6.1; M7 design §7.5). The fit and its residuals go into VehFootPrinter.info (§11.4).

docs.title: 9. Grid, M2 pass and reference heading
docs.text:
Inside locate(), before any chain runs: 1. M1 points for every row. Rows that fail the projection gate (§7.10) get NaN, not a point. 2. Grid: smoother.segment(m1, allow_missing=True) (§5.2). Every method uses this grid. Rows with an invalid projection keep their identity: - one invalid row (or a short run) between valid observations: it stays in the segment, unmeasured, fill_reason = "no_position"; - a run too long to bridge: the track splits there, and the run gets seg = −1; - an invalid prefix or suffix, or a track with no valid projection at all: seg = −1.

In every case these are box_rejected rows (§7.10): fp_fail starts with projection, and no box-derived ground point is invented for them. A box_rejected row inside a segment can still receive an admitted M7 pose (§7.7), and then fp_source = "M7" and fp_support = "kinematic". Otherwise fp_source = "none". seg = −1 rows are never admitted, and reach every later step with NaN outputs. 3. M2 points for every row with a valid projection. 4. Reference pass: smooth M2 on the grid (segmented=True), compute velocities, and apply the motion-heading rules (§10.1) to get ref_heading_deg. It is needed by M3, M4 (pair acceptance, front) and M7 (initial heading), and stored for M5/M6 axis direction.

Dropped from the study: the approach-direction fallback for tracks that never move (it needs movement labels, which tssa inputs do not carry). Those rows get NaN ψ_ref; M3 and M4 fail with no_heading; M7 starts from the path direction, as m7_runner._init_pose already does.

Segmentation basis. The study split on pixel jumps (0.5 box heights per frame, SPLIT_SPEED, SPLIT_LOGH). TrackSmoother splits on ground speed. The vehicle defaults in §11.3 use ground speed. The validation run (§14) counts segments against the study's grid and reports the difference. A pixel-jump rule in tssa.smooth is a follow-up, not part of this round.

docs.title: 10. Orientation and polygons (after smoothing)
docs.text: polygons(table) takes the SpeedCalculator output (the locate() columns, smoothed positions, vx, vy).

docs.title: 10.1 Motion heading
docs.text:
Units. The heading is unit-free, but the reliability threshold is not. - polygons(table, speed_unit=None) computes the speed itself from vx, vy. - Their unit is the speed_unit argument, else table.attrs["speed_unit"] ("mph" or "m/s", as SpeedCalculator writes it), and the threshold is converted to it. - If both are given and differ, or the unit is unknown, or neither is given: ValueError. Some pandas operations drop attrs, so the message says to pass speed_unit.

Per (track, seg) (base design §8.2): - heading_reliable at speed ≥ heading_min_mph (3); - otherwise hold the last reliable heading, and back-fill before the first; - a segment that is never reliable gets NaN motion heading (handled in §10.2).

docs.title: 10.2 Footprint orientation
docs.text:
Per (track, seg): 1. Native rows: those whose supplying locator gave an orientation (M3–M7). Every native orientation is folded to an axis for smoothing; the directed value is kept for step 4. 2. Axis smoothing, by the number n of native rows in the segment (as the study's smooth_orientation): - n = 0: no native axis; - n = 1: that axis, unchanged; - n ≥ 2: RTS on the doubled-angle unit vector (rts_smooth, guarded and correctly started, §5.3; orient_q 1.0, orient_sigma 0.1; study ORIENT_Q, ORIENT_SIGMA, both untuned). 3. Reach: the axis is used only within orient_reach_frames (10) of a native row (R10). 4. Direction of an axis, first available: 1. the row's motion heading (reliable, held or back-filled; §10.1). front_source = motion; 2. the segment never moves: the nearest directed native orientation in the segment (M7's ψ, M4's d_front, M3's ψ_ref). front_source = native; 3. the motion heading of the same track's nearest other segment in time. front_source = track; 4. none: the axis is kept with an arbitrary direction. front_source = none, front_known = False. 5. Rows without a native axis in reach use the motion heading, or else step 4.3. If neither exists, orient_deg is NaN and the row has no corners.

orient_source = native / motion / none. front_known is True unless step 4.4 was used.

Why fold, and when it matters. - While the vehicle moves, folding directed headings (M3, M4, M7) to axes loses nothing. M7's front rule is travel, so its front already faces the motion. For M4, the front correction already points d_front within 90° of ψ_ref. - A vehicle that never moves keeps its measured axis (step 4.2–4.4), so a parked bus with a passed M7 solve, or a stopped car with good M6 faces, still has an oriented footprint. Only its front may be unknown.

The directed native value stays in fp_orient_deg, and M4's m4_front_conflict and M7's m7_reversing remain as flags.

docs.title: 10.3 Size
docs.text: Per track and segment, in this order: 1. M7 passed solve (the segment's M7 solve has no fail reason): the solve's fitted L and W for every row of that segment (M7 design §9.3). dims_source = m7_measured / m7_partly_prior / m7_prior (M7 design §8.3, with the width-hold rule). 2. Measured classes (m6_measured_size_classes, default (2,)): the median M6 length and width over the track's M6 rows, when there are at least measured_size_min_rows (5; my call). dims_source = m6_measured. 3. Otherwise the class's nominal size (size_ft). dims_source = nominal.

docs.title: 10.4 Corners and output
docs.text:
corners = rect(centre = smoothed position, orient_deg, length, width), front-left first. Rows supplied by a point_only locator (M1), or without a smoothed position, get NaN corners and dims_source = none.

Added columns: motion_heading_deg, heading_reliable, orient_deg, orient_source, front_source, front_known, length_ft, width_ft, dims_source, c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, c3x, c3y, c4x, c4y (corners in world m). With front_known = False, the corner set is correct but which end is "front-left" is arbitrary.

VehFootPrinter.to_geodataframe(table, crs=None) returns one shapely polygon per row (empty where corners are NaN).

Low confidence (M7 design §9.6, combine_pet.low_confidence): fp_low_confidence = True on rows of a failed M7 solve that fell back, or on admitted kinematic rows more than lowconf_s (2.0 s) from the nearest supported row. This flag is what a PET step needs.

docs.title: 11.1 Construction and the main calls
docs.text:
from tssa.footprint import VehFootPrinter, FootprintConfig, detect
from tssa.transform import DistortedHomography

dh = DistortedHomography.load_json("model_a1a_nw.json")
tables = detect.run(video, tracks, detectors=[detect.KeypointDetector(),
                                              detect.CuboidDetector(uod_ckpt, uod_root),
                                              detect.MaskSegmenter(sam_ckpt)], cache_dir=cache)
vfp = VehFootPrinter(dh, zone=zone_from_points(gcps_utm, buffer_ft=15), workers=12, cache_dir=cache)

out = vfp.estimate(tracks, **tables)                 # locate -> smooth -> speed -> polygons
gdf = vfp.to_geodataframe(out, crs="EPSG:32617")

# infer only what this configuration needs (masks for buses and trucks only, with the default chains)
tables = detect.run(video, tracks, detectors=[...], rows=vfp.required_rows(tracks), cache_dir=cache)

class VehFootPrinter:
    def __init__(self, homography, config: FootprintConfig | None = None, image_size=None, zone=None,
                 camera=None, smoother: TrackSmoother | None = None, speed: SpeedCalculator | None = None,
                 workers: int = 1, cache_dir=None, **config_overrides) -> None: ...
    def locate(self, tracks, only_tracks=None, **tables) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def polygons(self, table, speed_unit=None) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def required_rows(self, tracks, only_tracks=None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]: ...
    def estimate(self, tracks, only_tracks=None, **tables) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    def compare(self, tracks, methods=("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7"), fallback="M2",
                admit_kinematic=None, only_tracks=None, **tables) -> pd.DataFrame: ...
    @staticmethod
    def to_geodataframe(table, crs=None): ...
    @staticmethod
    def available_locators() -> dict[str, dict]: ...
    info: dict      # camera fit and consistency, grid counts, M7 solve summaries (one row per solve)
  • homography, image_size: wrapped in GroundModel (§4.2); construction fails without an image size.
  • camera: pass a fitted PinholeCamera to skip the fit.
  • smoother: a user smoother must use xy_cols=("fp_x", "fp_y") and cov_cols=("fp_cov_xx", "fp_cov_xy", "fp_cov_yy"); anything else raises ValueError at construction, so the fill-scaling rule of §7.9 cannot be bypassed by accident.
  • **tables: the detection tables by name, so a later locator needs no new parameter.
  • Errors raise ValueError early, as the existing classes do: bad config, an unknown locator name, a chain naming an unregistered locator, a column clash, a table missing its columns.

docs.title: 11.2 compare()
docs.text:
Runs each method as a single-locator chain on the same grid and reference heading, smooths and polygons each, and returns one long table with a method column.

Modes. One precedence rule for admit_kinematic in compare():

fallback admit_kinematic Result None (native-only) None or False admission off None (native-only) True ValueError: admission contradicts native-only set (end-to-end) None config.admit_kinematic (default True) set (end-to-end) True / False as given
  • Native-only means measurements of the method's own observations only. A kinematic M7 row has no measurement: fp_source = none, fp_support empty, fp_fail = "M7:no_observation", while m7_support = kinematic stays in the extras.
  • End-to-end (base design §7, without eligibility): admitted rows have fp_source = M7 and fp_support = kinematic; rows the method fails on take the fallback.

Row contract: every input row, once per method. No row is ever dropped, so the per-method tables pair row by row. - Rows a method does not cover keep their identity, with fp_source = none and fp_fail = "<method>:class_ineligible". Today that is M7 on classes outside m7_classes, such as cars. - The fallback is not applied to class_ineligible rows. An "M7 end-to-end" car would otherwise be pure M2 under the M7 label, and paired M7-vs-M6 comparisons on cars would compare M2 with M6. - Rows outside only_tracks are present with fp_source = none and fp_fail = "excluded".

It is what a project needs to rebuild the study's comparison: offsets between methods, speed traps, its own metrics.

docs.title: 11.3 Vehicle defaults inside estimate()
docs.text:
TrackSmoother's defaults are tuned for pedestrians: they would cut vehicle tracks at every frame faster than 6 m/s (13 mph). When no smoother is passed, VehFootPrinter builds:

TrackSmoother("rts", params={"q": 2.0},                 # study RTS_Q, m²/s³ (gap regression: turn error 0.116 mph)
              xy_cols=("fp_x", "fp_y"), cov_cols=("fp_cov_xx", "fp_cov_xy", "fp_cov_yy"),
              fps=config.fps, split_speed=30.0,         # m/s (~67 mph): a jump or id switch; my call, §9
              fill_max_gap=20, gap_max_speed=26.8)      # frames; m/s = 60 mph (study FILL_MAX_GAP, GAP_MAX_SPEED_MPH)
SpeedCalculator(fps=config.fps, xy_cols=("fp_x_smooth", "fp_y_smooth"))   # mph, the tssa default

estimate() calls smoother.smooth(loc, segmented=True) on locate()'s output (§5.2): no re-segmentation, every row returned, and rows without a reference point unmeasured. polygons() reads the speed unit from the calculator's attrs (§10.1). estimate() passes it explicitly, so the result does not depend on attrs surviving.

docs.title: 11.4 info
docs.text: The camera (f, cx, cy, height, consistency RMS/max), segment and fill counts, per-locator success and failure counts, and the M7 per-solve table (study m7_tracks.csv columns). These are what the study's manifest recorded and what a user needs to judge a run.

docs.title: 12.2 M7Config
docs.text: A frozen dataclass holding every M7_* setting of the study's settings.py as of 2026-11-10, with the same values and their comments as docstrings. These include the prior sets (bus, truck, pickup/van), subtypes, loose width priors, inset priors, gates, σ values, solver iteration limits, front rule, width hold and pair start. The study code reads module globals (S.M7_*); the port passes an M7Config instead. Its hash enters the solve cache key.

Helpers stay inside footprint/ (AGENTS.md: keep packages narrowly scoped); engine/ is not touched.

Lazy OpenCV in homography.py (review comment 6: today it imports cv2 at module load, so import tssa.transform fails without OpenCV): - import cv2 moves into the functions that fit (cv2.findHomography). - Projection (_project) becomes the homogeneous product in numpy, replacing cv2.perspectiveTransform. It must agree with the current results to 1e-9 on the existing test_homography cases, and those tests must pass unchanged. - The constructor default method: int = cv2.RANSAC becomes method: int | None = None, meaning RANSAC, resolved inside the fit. Passing OpenCV constants still works. - Guarantee: load_json / load_matrix and both projection directions work without OpenCV; constructing a homography from point pairs needs it.

Provenance. Every ported file starts with a docstring naming its study source file and that file's SHA-256, as listed in the snapshot manifest (§17, phase 0). The manifest, not the per-file docstrings, establishes that all ported files come from one state.

docs.title: 14.1 Ported synthetic tests
docs.text:
The study's suite had 210 tests for M1–M6 and 53 more for M7 at the last count. The method tests are ported with their fixtures: - test_geometry, test_m3; - test_m4: frontal/rear/oblique; the unequal-overhang bus under all four label permutations to 1e-6 ft; malformed-pair rejection; camera-away success; misaligned far pairs; head-on side_ambiguous; reversing bus; elevated hub to 0.05 ft; - test_m5, test_m6, test_camera; - test_m7 and test_m7_candidates, using m7_synth.py: the 40 ft bus on a 90° right turn with 0.5 px noise, the association examples of test 21, and the rest; - the parts of test_smooth covering motion heading and orientation smoothing.

Tests of the study's evaluation machinery (products, metrics, stops, sampling, clips, export) are not ported (§2).

docs.title: 14.2 New tests
docs.text:
tssa.smooth (§5) 1. Covariance: - cov_cols with R = σ²I gives the same result as sigma_col = σ on interp = 0 rows; - on interp = 1 rows the covariance is not inflated, while sigma_col is (§5.1); - a non-PD R raises; - the existing smoother tests pass unchanged. 2. Segmenting with missing positions (allow_missing=True, review comment 1): - one invalid row between valid observations stays in its segment, unmeasured, fill_reason = "no_position"; - an invalid run longer than fill_max_gap splits the track and gets seg = −1; - an invalid prefix and an invalid suffix get seg = −1; - a track with no valid position is returned whole, with seg = −1; - every input row is returned once. 3. Segmented smoothing (review comment 2): - stale positions: segment on M1 positions, then smooth M6 positions that are deliberately offset by 3 m. The output follows M6, not M1, for rts, ma and sg, and for a 1-row segment; - large origin, two tolerances, both absolute (rtol = 0; a default relative tolerance at UTM scale would hide millimetres), on coordinates with six decimals (e.g. 5200000.123456 m): - internal: the local ↔ world conversion, before output rounding, round-trips to 1e-6 m; - public: the returned <pos>_smooth columns are within 0.0005 m. The smoother rounds its added columns to three decimals in _finish(), and segmented mode keeps that rounding, the same as the legacy path. No output precision changes. - failed method: with every position NaN, a segment returns NaN and fallback = 1, without raising; - structural columns: input with seg/fill_reason does not clash, and a non-consecutive segment raises. 4. Admission (review comment 3): an M7 point on an inserted interp = 2 frame changes the smoothed result; the same table with that point removed does not use it. 5. rts_smooth: - 0 and 1 measured rows raise ValueError; - exact constant-velocity data with a 10-frame missing prefix recovers frame 0 to 1e-6 m (today: 1.54 m off); - segments that start with a measurement give the same result as before.

Ground model and camera (§4.2, §8)

  1. Adapter:
  2. a HomographyTransform has identity distortion and needs an explicit image_size;
  3. a DistortedHomography gives its own size, and a conflicting explicit size raises;
  4. an object with only undistort raises.
  5. Camera fit: fits through both an ordinary and a distorted homography (synthetic radial distortion), with consistency residuals under 1e-6 px on exact data.
  6. Lazy imports (review comment 6), with cv2, torch and ultralytics blocked in sys.modules:
  7. import tssa, tssa.transform and tssa.footprint;
  8. DistortedHomography.load_json of a saved model, and projection in both directions;
  9. PinholeCamera.fit;
  10. an M2-only and an M6-only estimate().

Fitting a homography and running M5 raise ImportError naming OpenCV.

Footprint

  1. Chains:
  2. a truck row: M7 failed solve → collapsed M6 face → M3 → with no heading, M2; fp_fail lists each failure in order;
  3. a car without cuboids: M6:not_supplied, then M2.
  4. Covariance per support type (§7.9): an interp = 1 box row has 16 · R; an admitted M7 row has exactly the §7.7 covariance.
  5. Size: an M7 passed segment uses the fitted L and W on every row, fallback rows included; a car with 5 M6 rows uses their median, with 4 nominal; a bus is always nominal unless M7 passed.
  6. Orientation (review comment 4):
    • no native axes: the motion heading is used, without error;
    • one native axis: that axis within reach;
    • an axis around 179°/1° never smooths to 90°;
    • the reach rule;
    • direction toward motion.
  7. Never-moving vehicles (review comment 5):
    • a stationary car with M6 faces keeps the M6 axis. front_source is track when another segment of the track moves, otherwise none with front_known = False. Corners are present either way;
    • a stationary M7 bus takes its direction from ψ (front_source = native);
    • a car that waits, then drives: the waiting rows are back-filled from the first moving heading (front_source = motion).
  8. Speed units (review comment 8): one track through SpeedCalculator(units="metric") and units="imperial" gives identical heading_reliable and orient_deg. A table without attrs and without speed_unit raises.
  9. compare() (first review 9 and 10; second review 3):
    • fallback=None:
    • with admit_kinematic=None and with False: the kinematic M7 row has no measurement, fp_source = none, fp_support empty, fp_fail = "M7:no_observation", and m7_support = kinematic stays;
    • with True: ValueError;
    • fallback="M2":
    • with admit_kinematic=None (config default True) and with True: the same row is admitted, fp_source = M7, fp_support = kinematic;
    • with False: it takes M2;
    • a mixed car/bus input returns every row once per method, with M7 car rows class_ineligible and no fallback, in both modes;
    • only_tracks rows are excluded.
  10. End to end: a straight car and a turning car rendered to boxes and cuboid faces through a synthetic camera with 0.5 px noise and a 15-frame hole. The centre is within 0.3 ft, the heading within 2°, and the speed within 0.2 mph of truth (base design §8.2 bound).
  11. Every input row returned once by locate() and estimate(), including invalid-projection rows.
  12. Admission through the real pipeline (second review 1). estimate() runs on a synthetic bus with a passed M7 solve (a stub M7 locator in phase 2, the real one in phase 5), whose segment contains:
    • an inserted gap frame (interp = 2, NaN box fields, no Jacobian): it is admitted, fp_row_kind = inserted, and its fp_cov_* equal the §7.7 covariance exactly. The smoothed position moves toward the M7 pose compared with the same run with admit_kinematic=False;
    • an original box_rejected row inside the segment with kinematic support: it is admitted, and fp_fail still starts with projection;
    • an original box_rejected row with native M7 support: not used by M7, so the next locator in the chain is tried;
    • a seg = −1 prefix row: never admitted, NaN outputs.
  13. Width hold (second review 2): w_ft_per_px = 0.29, exactly 0.3, 0.31 and inf, with threshold 0.3, gives held = False, False, True, True, and None as the threshold never holds. This is the same decision as the study's expression, evaluated on those inputs.

Detectors (§6)

  1. Matching: a dense frame with crossing boxes is assigned one-to-one; an IoU under 0.3 is unmatched.
  2. Row selection (review comment 11):
    • required_rows with a custom car chain containing M5 lists car rows under masks;
    • the default chains list only cls 5/7 rows there;
    • in a crowded frame, requesting one track's rows gives the same match as requesting all rows (matching context is the whole frame). This is tested with a fake detector, so no model is needed.

docs.title: 16. Decisions on the open points (user, 2026-11-10)
docs.text:
• Q6. Freeze point for M7: snapshot now. The user has reviewed the M7 clips, so the snapshot (§17, phase 0) is taken now. The study's code has not changed since run 20261110_161113_s0: the newest code file is settings.py (2026-11-10 16:10, just before that run), and the later edit to the M7 notes (18:50) only reports that run. The snapshot is therefore exactly the state §7.6 describes. Later study changes are ported deliberately, each with a new snapshot and a validation rerun.
  • Q7. Method names: M1–M7 only, for now. Descriptive aliases (bottom_centre, nominal_shift, nominal_box, wheel_keypoints, sam_outline, cuboid, wheel_fit) are added later, as a follow-up outside phases 0–6. (Done in 0.0.2.12, §7.8.) The registry (§7.1) must therefore allow more than one name per locator without changing its result columns: fp_source keeps the canonical M name.

docs.title: 17. Build order
docs.text:
Each phase ends with its tests passing and a commit. The version bumps by one patch per phase.

  1. Study snapshot (review: source handoff). A read-only archive of the study folder's code, documents and settings, plus docs/study-snapshot-<date>.json committed in tssa. The manifest records:
  2. every .py and .md file with its SHA-256;
  3. the full settings.py values;
  4. the column schemas and one example row of each cache table (m4, m5, m6, m7, m7solve);
  5. pip freeze of the study's Python 3.14 environment, and the model checkpoint hashes;
  6. the run directories used in §14.3.

Code is ported only from the archive. Taken now (Q6, §16). 1. tssa.transform and tssa.smooth foundations: - lazy OpenCV in homography.py and the GroundModel adapter (§4.2, §13); - cov_cols, segment(allow_missing), smooth(segmented) and the rts_smooth fixes (§5); - tests 1–6, plus test 8 for the transform part; - the existing smooth, speed and homography tests unchanged. 2. Core footprint: config, geometry, registry, M1–M3, M6, chains, grid and reference pass, orientation, polygons, estimate(), compare(); ported tests for geometry, M3 and M6; tests 9–18 (M7 parts with a stub locator). 3. Camera and M4, M5: transform/camera.py without OpenCV, M4, M5, masks.py; ported tests; test 7; the rest of test 8. 4. Detectors: match.py, detect/ with cache, required_rows(); tests 20–21; detector check of §14.3. 5. M7: candidates, solver, runner with workers and cache, admission, low-confidence flag; ported M7 tests; tests 4, 10, 13, 15 and 18 against the real locator; test 19. 6. Validation run (§14.3); results into §19; README.md section; pyproject.toml extra detect.

docs.title: 18. Left to the builder
docs.text:
• LocatorResult and LocateContext field details.
  • How M7's process pool is started on Windows (spawn) and on Linux.
  • Whether split_speed = 30 m/s needs changing after the §14.3 segment count; reported either way.
  • Whether to vectorise M3 and M5 (the study solves them row by row).

docs.title: 19. Validation results (NW clip, 2026-11-11)
docs.text:
Run with docs/validation/nw_clip_validation.py (parts native, grid, e2e, trap, m7, m7study, m7compare, estimate) and docs/validation/detector_check.py, on the pinned inputs of §14.3 and the study code from the snapshot (§17 phase 0). The port ran on Linux (WSL2, Python 3.12, scipy 1.17); the study's reports were made on Windows (Python 3.14).

Check Result Verdict Camera f 319.5459, (cx, cy) (334.1009, 240.1256), height 6.7331 m; largest difference from the study 5e-8 pass M1, M2, M3, M6 native points 46,213 / 46,213 / 46,213 / 34,628 rows valid in both, none in one only; max difference 0 m pass M4 native points 2,364 rows valid in both; max difference 1.4e-9 m; label_case and interior_source equal pass M4 counts (metric psi_ref) 2,185 valid (2,175 camera_away, 10 other_pair); front_conflict on tracks 230 and 432 pass M5 (solve_m5 on the study's outlines) 23,526 rows valid in both, no disagreement, max difference 0 m pass M7 port vs the study's solver, same jobs, same machine 25 / 25 same pass/fail and reason; 17 passed; L and W differences 0 ft on all pass M7 port vs the study's run report (20261110_161113_s0) 23 / 25 same pass/fail (315 param_bound and 452 wheel_resid here, passed there); on the 17 passed in both, |dL| median 0.11 ft, max 2.97 ft (track 176), 6 within 0.05 ft; |dW| max 0.21 ft platform noise, see below Detectors, 200 sampled rows keypoints 66 / 66 rows, max 0.15 px; cuboid corners 66 / 66, max 0.05 px; masks 68 / 68 with IoU ≥ 0.99 (min 0.99996) after the 5% component rule; M5 lower outlines from the port's single SAM pass identical to the study's M5 cache on 200 / 200 rows pass Grid 445 segments here, 732 in the study (426 labelled tracks) reported, see below Smoothed M6 centres vs the study's M6 display 32,852 rows; median 0.0014 ft, p95 0.18 ft reported Speed trap, NB/SB through vehicles common to both |error| p90 (mph) here / study: M1 0.332 / 0.332, M2 0.365 / 0.365, M3 0.384 / 0.385, M4 0.365 / 0.361, M6 0.384 / 0.384; medians within 0.006 mph pass (study's 0.38 mph)

M7 and the platform. The study's own solver, run on the same jobs on the Linux machine, gives exactly the port's results, and differs from its Windows report in the same way the port does (the two pass/fail flips, the same |dL| per track). The Windows-vs-Linux difference is most likely floating-point differences in the least-squares path (BLAS, scipy version; not traced further): the fit is multi-start with pruning, so a small change in one start's final cost can change which start wins. The 0.05 ft gate of §14.3 therefore holds on one platform, not across platforms; across platforms expect a median |dL| near 0.1 ft, rare multi-foot outliers, and some pass/fail changes (2 of 25 here).

Grid. Ground-speed segmentation (§9, §15) cuts far less than the study's pixel-jump rule. Of the study's 306 cuts inside tracks, 292 are between consecutive frames, at a median box jump of 20 px (1.3 m), and 257 of its 732 segments have 5 rows or fewer. Lowering split_speed does not reproduce the study's grid: 456 segments at 20 m/s; 558 at 15 m/s, with 41 tracks cut less and 40 cut more than the study; 2,589 at 10 m/s. §18's question is answered: keep 30 m/s. The coarser grid does not move the smoothed centres materially (row above) and leaves the speed trap unchanged on common vehicles.

Speed trap, all vehicles. On every NB/SB through vehicle (251 to 254 per method, against the study's 139 to 167 eligible ones), the p90 is 0.375 to 0.461 mph; the study's eligibility rules (§15, first row) are not applied here.

estimate() with the default chains. On the 426 labelled tracks (54,241 rows), with every detection table, 21 minutes with 10 workers (0.0.2.10, nothing cached). Sources: M6 33,650 rows, M2 10,555, M7 1,980, M3 28, none 8,028 (rejected projections). M7 solved the 25 bus and truck segments of the port's grid: 16 passed, 4 param_bound, 3 articulated_suspect, 2 wheel_resid (these segments are cut by §9, not the study's display segments, so the 17 / 25 above is not directly comparable). On bus and truck rows: M7 1,980 (18 of them admitted kinematic), M6 798, M2 735, M3 28; sizes m7_measured 394, m7_partly_prior 1,106, m7_prior 480, nominal 1,579. fp_low_confidence is set on 1,579 rows, the fallback rows of the failed solves. Speed trap on all 253 NB/SB through vehicles: |error| median 0.20 mph, p90 0.45 mph.

M7 speed (0.0.2.10). The 0.0.2.9 solver (the study's algorithm as ported) took about 2 minutes per 70 to 90-frame segment on one uncontended core, and up to 20 minutes per segment with 10 to 16 solves sharing the machine. Two changes leave the results unchanged (the 25 display solves are identical in pass/fail, F, L and W): a finite-difference Jacobian computed in grouped evaluations that equals scipy's sparse 2-point Jacobian bit for bit (tested), and racing (from outer round 4, a start, pair restart or cross refit is dropped while its cost is more than 5% above the best finished fit). One segment uncontended: 113 s to 53 s (88 frames) and 132 s to 62 s (69 frames). Cheaper search settings (M7_COARSE_OUTER, M7_SEARCH_TOL) saved only 11% more and changed 3 pass/fail outcomes, so they are off by default. The runner gives each worker one BLAS thread; more workers than physical cores lengthens every solve.

• Descriptive aliases for the footprint methods: bottom_centre (M1), nominal_shift (M2), nominal_box (M3), wheel_keypoints (M4), sam_outline (M5), cuboid (M6), wheel_fit (M7). They are accepted in chains, default_chain and compare(methods=..., fallback=...); outputs keep the M names.
  • register_alias(), and register_locator(aliases=...) for your own methods.

• Validation of VehFootPrinter on the NW clip against the speed study, recorded in §19 of the footprint design.
  • README section on vehicle footprints.
• M7 is about 2.1x faster with the same results: a grouped finite-difference Jacobian (identical to SciPy's) and racing of the fit candidates (M7_RACE_ROUND, M7_RACE_MARGIN).
• M7, the wheel-anchored rigid fit for buses and trucks, with parallel solves (workers) and a solve cache (cache_dir).
• tssa.footprint.detect: keypoint, cuboid and SAM mask detectors, one-to-one matching to track boxes, and a cached runner that reads the video once.
• M4 (wheel keypoints) and M5 (mask outline), the MaskTable, and the pinhole camera fit.
• tssa.footprint.VehFootPrinter with M1-M3 and M6, per-class fallback chains and per-row covariance.
• Segmented smoothing (segment() once, smooth(segmented=True) many times), per-row covariance columns, and GroundModel.
• tssa.speed.SpeedCalculator; TrackSmoother now returns positions only.

• tssa.smooth.TrackSmoother.
  • DistortedHomography in tssa.transform.
• Version 0.0.1.0.
• Count and spatial calculation; track-zone matching and lane detection followed in October 2024.

docs.title: Vehicle footprints and speed
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from tssa.footprint import VehFootPrinter, detect, zone_from_points
from tssa.transform import DistortedHomography

dh = DistortedHomography.load_json("model_a1a_nw.json")       # no OpenCV needed to load and project
tracks = pd.read_csv("veh_tracks.csv")                         # frame, track, x, y, w, h, cls (pixels)
gcps = pd.read_csv("gcps.csv")[["utm_e_m", "utm_n_m"]].to_numpy()
vfp = VehFootPrinter(dh, zone=zone_from_points(gcps, buffer_ft=15), workers=8, cache_dir="cache")

# optional: run the detectors (pip install tssa[detect]) for the rows the default chains need
tables = detect.run("clip.mp4", tracks,
                    [detect.KeypointDetector(), detect.CuboidDetector("uod.pt", "path/to/urbanomnidetect"),
                     detect.MaskSegmenter("sam2.1_b.pt")],
                    rows=vfp.required_rows(tracks), cache_dir="cache")

out = vfp.estimate(tracks, **tables)                           # reference point, smoothed position, speed, polygon
gdf = vfp.to_geodataframe(out, crs="EPSG:32617")               # one polygon per row, for PET
  • tracks has one row per box: frame, track, x, y, w, h in pixels of the original (distorted) image, and cls. Rename the columns with box_cols= and cls_col=.
  • Without detections, the default chains fall back to the methods that need none (M2, and M3 for trucks).
  • Without a zone no camera is fitted, so M4 and M7 are skipped and their rows go to the next method in the chain.

docs.title: Choosing methods
docs.text:
Each class has a chain of methods, tried in order until one places the row:

vfp = VehFootPrinter(dh, zone=zone, chains={2: ("cuboid", "nominal_shift"), 7: ("M7", "M3", "M2")})

Methods can be named M1-M7 or by their aliases (bottom_centre, nominal_shift, nominal_box, wheel_keypoints, sam_outline, cuboid, wheel_fit). Outputs always carry the M names.

To compare methods on the same rows:

long = vfp.compare(tracks, methods=("M2", "M6", "M7"), fallback=None, **tables)   # each method's own rows only
long.groupby("method")["fp_source"].apply(lambda s: s.ne("none").mean())   # share of rows each method placed

docs.title: Reading the output
docs.text:
Every input row appears once, plus the rows inserted to fill gaps (fp_row_kind == "inserted").

Columns Meaning fp_x, fp_y, fp_cov_xx, fp_cov_xy, fp_cov_yy, fp_sigma Reference point (world m) and its covariance, before smoothing fp_source, fp_support, fp_fail Which method placed the row, native or kinematic, and why the earlier methods failed fp_x_smooth, fp_y_smooth, vx, vy, speed Smoothed position and speed (mph by default) orient_deg, motion_heading_deg, length_ft, width_ft, dims_source Orientation, heading and size of the polygon c1x ... c4y The four corners (world m) fp_low_confidence The polygon should not be trusted for PET

docs.title: Smoothing and speed on their own
docs.text:
If you already have ground positions in metres:

from tssa.smooth import TrackSmoother
from tssa.speed import SpeedCalculator

sm = TrackSmoother(method="rts", fps=10)                       # or "sg7", "ma", or method="sg", params={"win": 9}
smoothed = sm.smooth(ground_tracks)                            # adds seg, fill_reason, x_smooth, y_smooth, fallback
speeds = SpeedCalculator(fps=10, xy_cols=("x_smooth", "y_smooth")).calculate(smoothed)

docs.title: Fitting a homography
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from tssa.transform import DistortedHomography

g = pd.read_csv("gcps.csv")                                    # pixel u, v and world utm_e_m, utm_n_m
dh = DistortedHomography(g[["u", "v"]].to_numpy(), g[["utm_e_m", "utm_n_m"]].to_numpy(), image_size=(1920, 1080))
dh.save_json("model.json")                                     # fitting needs OpenCV; loading does not

kmz_to_csv converts Google Earth placemarks into a CSV of latitude and longitude. Project them to UTM (or State Plane) before fitting.
