Source code in src/tssa/footprint/geometry.py 
def edge_flag(boxes, image_size, edge_px: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Box within edge_px of an image border."""
    b = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(boxes, dtype=float))
    W, H = image_size
    x, y, w, h = b.T
    return (x < edge_px) | (y < edge_px) | (x + w > W - edge_px) | (y + h > H - edge_px)

docs.title: rect_corners
docs.text:
rect_corners(centre, heading_deg, L_m, W_m) -> np.ndarray

Corners front-left, front-right, rear-right, rear-left (front along the heading).

One rectangle: centre (2,), scalar heading -> (4, 2). Vectorised: centre (n, 2), heading (n,), L and W broadcastable to (n,) -> (n, 4, 2).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/geometry.py 
def rect_corners(centre, heading_deg, L_m, W_m) -> np.ndarray:
    """Corners front-left, front-right, rear-right, rear-left (front along the heading).

    One rectangle: centre (2,), scalar heading -> (4, 2). Vectorised: centre (n, 2), heading (n,), L and W
    broadcastable to (n,) -> (n, 4, 2).
    """
    c = np.asarray(centre, dtype=float)
    f = unit_from_compass(heading_deg)
    lf = rot_ccw(f)
    L = np.asarray(L_m, dtype=float)
    W = np.asarray(W_m, dtype=float)
    if c.ndim == 1:
        a, b = L / 2.0 * f, W / 2.0 * lf
        return np.array([c + a + b, c + a - b, c - a - b, c - a + b])
    a = (L.reshape(-1, 1) / 2.0) * f
    b = (W.reshape(-1, 1) / 2.0) * lf
    return np.stack([c + a + b, c + a - b, c - a - b, c - a + b], axis=1)

docs.title: face_geometry
docs.text:
face_geometry(face_uv, ground)

Cuboid bottom face (4 image corners, any start or winding) -> (corners (4, 2), centroid, length_m, width_m, axis_deg): opposite-edge means give length and width, the doubled-angle mean of the long edges the axis.

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/geometry.py 
def face_geometry(face_uv, ground):
    """Cuboid bottom face (4 image corners, any start or winding) -> (corners (4, 2), centroid, length_m, width_m,
    axis_deg): opposite-edge means give length and width, the doubled-angle mean of the long edges the axis."""
    corners = project(ground, np.asarray(face_uv, dtype=float).reshape(4, 2))
    edges = np.roll(corners, -1, axis=0) - corners  # edge i: corner i -> i + 1
    lens = np.linalg.norm(edges, axis=1)
    pair_a, pair_b = lens[[0, 2]].mean(), lens[[1, 3]].mean()
    long_i = (0, 2) if pair_a >= pair_b else (1, 3)
    length, width = max(pair_a, pair_b), min(pair_a, pair_b)
    ang = np.radians(compass_deg(edges[list(long_i)]))
    axis = to_undirected(np.degrees(np.arctan2(np.sin(2 * ang).sum(), np.cos(2 * ang).sum())) / 2.0)
    return corners, corners.mean(axis=0), float(length), float(width), float(axis)

docs.text: Motion heading rules and native-axis smoothing (design docs/2026-11-10-footprint-design.md section 10; ported from the speed study's smooth.py and products.py).

docs.title: motion_heading
docs.text:
motion_heading(
    vel, min_speed
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Directed heading per row of ONE segment and its reliability, from smoothed velocity (any unit; min_speed in the same unit). Unreliable rows hold the last reliable heading; rows before the first reliable one are back-filled from it; a segment with no reliable row gets NaN everywhere.

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/orientation.py 
def motion_heading(vel, min_speed) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Directed heading per row of ONE segment and its reliability, from smoothed velocity (any unit; `min_speed` in
    the same unit). Unreliable rows hold the last reliable heading; rows before the first reliable one are
    back-filled from it; a segment with no reliable row gets NaN everywhere."""
    vel = np.asarray(vel, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    speed = np.hypot(vel[:, 0], vel[:, 1])
    reliable = np.isfinite(speed) & (speed >= min_speed)
    n = len(vel)
    if not reliable.any():
        return np.full(n, np.nan), reliable
    raw = np.where(reliable, compass_deg(np.where(reliable[:, None], vel, 1.0)), np.nan)
    idx = np.where(reliable, np.arange(n), -1)
    idx = np.maximum.accumulate(idx)  # last reliable row at or before each row
    idx[idx < 0] = np.flatnonzero(reliable)[0]  # back-fill
    return raw[idx], reliable

docs.title: smooth_axis
docs.text:
smooth_axis(
    deg, has, q: float, sigma: float, dt: float
) -> np.ndarray

Smooth the native axes of ONE segment (rows has) in doubled-angle form; result in [0, 180), every row.

0 native rows: all NaN. 1: that axis on every row. 2 or more: RTS on the doubled-angle unit vector (rows without a native axis are predicted). The reach rule is applied by the caller.

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/orientation.py 
def smooth_axis(deg, has, q: float, sigma: float, dt: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Smooth the native axes of ONE segment (rows `has`) in doubled-angle form; result in [0, 180), every row.

    0 native rows: all NaN. 1: that axis on every row. 2 or more: RTS on the doubled-angle unit vector (rows without
    a native axis are predicted). The reach rule is applied by the caller.
    """
    deg = np.asarray(deg, dtype=float)
    has = np.asarray(has, dtype=bool) & np.isfinite(deg)
    n = len(deg)
    k = int(has.sum())
    if k == 0:
        return np.full(n, np.nan)
    if k == 1:
        return np.full(n, deg[has][0] % 180.0)
    th = np.radians(deg * 2.0)
    vec = np.column_stack([np.cos(th), np.sin(th)])
    vec[~has] = np.nan
    R = np.tile(np.eye(2) * sigma**2, (n, 1, 1))
    sm, _ = rts_smooth(vec, R, dt, q)
    out = (np.degrees(np.arctan2(sm[:, 1], sm[:, 0])) / 2.0) % 180.0
    return np.where(out >= 180.0, 0.0, out)

def near(frames, has, reach: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """True on rows within `reach` frames of a row with `has` (one segment, frames sorted)."""
    frames = np.asarray(frames)
    has = np.asarray(has, dtype=bool)
    if not has.any():
        return np.zeros(len(frames), bool)
    return nearest_distance(frames, frames[has]) <= reach

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/orientation.py 
def nearest_distance(frames, targets) -> np.ndarray:
    """Distance (frames) from each frame to the nearest of the sorted `targets`."""
    frames = np.asarray(frames)
    targets = np.asarray(targets)
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(targets, frames), 1, max(len(targets) - 1, 1))
    lo = targets[np.minimum(k - 1, len(targets) - 1)]
    hi = targets[np.minimum(k, len(targets) - 1)]
    return np.minimum(np.abs(frames - lo), np.abs(frames - hi))

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/orientation.py 
def nearest_index(frames, targets) -> np.ndarray:
    """Index into the sorted `targets` of the nearest one to each frame."""
    frames = np.asarray(frames)
    targets = np.asarray(targets)
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(targets, frames), 1, max(len(targets) - 1, 1))
    lo, hi = np.minimum(k - 1, len(targets) - 1), np.minimum(k, len(targets) - 1)
    return np.where(np.abs(frames - targets[lo]) <= np.abs(frames - targets[hi]), lo, hi)

Method Alias Needs Scope Classes M1 bottom_centre - row (point only) all M2 nominal_shift - row all M3 nominal_box - row all M4 wheel_keypoints keypoints, camera row all M5 sam_outline masks row all M6 cuboid cuboids row all M7 wheel_fit masks, camera segment 5 (bus), 7 (truck)

docs.title: locators
docs.text:
Locator registry: a locator turns rows (bbox, class, extra tables) into native reference points.

Design docs/2026-11-10-footprint-design.md, section 7.1. A locator is registered with

@register_locator("M5", needs=("masks",), scope="row", point_only=False)
def locate_m5(rows: pd.DataFrame, ctx: LocateContext) -> LocatorResult: ...
  • scope "row": rows are original rows with a valid projection (fp_row_kind == "box"), any subset.
  • scope "segment": rows are whole segments (consecutive frames, inserted rows included) of one class.
  • classes: the cls_track values the locator serves (None = all); other rows fail with "class_ineligible".
  • A locator whose needs tables were not supplied fails every row with "not_supplied".
  • aliases: further names that resolve to the locator (design 16, Q7), such as "cuboid" for M6. Chains and compare() accept either; results always carry the canonical name (fp_source, fp_fail, method).

rows carries: track, frame, the box columns (x, y, w, h under their configured names, NaN on inserted rows), cls_track, seg, interp, fp_row_kind, u_bc, v_bc (bbox bottom-centre px), m1_x, m1_y, m2_x, m2_y (world m) and ref_heading_deg.

def register_locator(name: str, needs=(), scope: str = "row", point_only: bool = False, classes=None, aliases=()):
    """Decorator: register `fn(rows, ctx) -> LocatorResult` as locator `name`, also reachable as each of `aliases`."""
    if scope not in ("row", "segment"):
        raise ValueError(f"scope must be 'row' or 'segment', got {scope!r}")
    if name in ALIASES:
        raise ValueError(f"{name!r} is already an alias of {ALIASES[name]!r}")
    aliases = (aliases,) if isinstance(aliases, str) else tuple(aliases)

    def wrap(fn):
        REGISTRY[name] = Locator(name, fn, tuple(needs), scope, bool(point_only),
                                 None if classes is None else tuple(classes))  # fmt: skip
        for a in aliases:
            register_alias(a, name)
        return fn

    return wrap

def register_alias(alias: str, name: str) -> None:
    """Make `alias` another name of the registered locator `name`."""
    if name not in REGISTRY:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown locator {name!r}; known: {sorted(REGISTRY)}")
    if alias in REGISTRY:
        raise ValueError(f"{alias!r} is a locator name, not available as an alias")
    if ALIASES.get(alias, name) != name:
        raise ValueError(f"{alias!r} is already an alias of {ALIASES[alias]!r}")
    ALIASES[alias] = name

def canonical(name: str) -> str:
    """The registered name behind `name` (itself, or the locator an alias points to); ValueError if unknown."""
    if name in REGISTRY:
        return name
    if name in ALIASES and ALIASES[name] in REGISTRY:
        return ALIASES[name]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown locator {name!r}; known: {sorted(REGISTRY)}, aliases: {sorted(ALIASES)}")

@register_locator("M1", point_only=True, aliases="bottom_centre")
def locate_m1(rows, ctx) -> LocatorResult:
    """The world point under the bbox bottom-centre: the foot of the box, not the body centre."""
    res = LocatorResult.empty(len(rows))
    xy = rows[["m1_x", "m1_y"]].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(xy).all(axis=1)
    res.ok, res.x, res.y = ok, xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1]
    res.fail_reason[~ok] = "projection"
    return res

def solve_m3(ground, box_xywh, heading_deg, L_m, W_m, init, resid_ok_px: float = 0.5):
    """(centre, corners, ok, resid_px): the nominal rectangle at `heading_deg` whose projection has its lowest point
    on the bbox bottom and its horizontal midpoint at the bbox centre (distorted pixels, like the bbox)."""
    nan2, nan42 = np.full(2, np.nan), np.full((4, 2), np.nan)
    init = np.asarray(init, dtype=float)
    if not np.isfinite(heading_deg) or not np.isfinite(init).all():
        return nan2, nan42, False, np.nan
    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in box_xywh)
    tv, tu = y + h, x + w / 2.0

    def resid(d):
        uv = np.asarray(ground.world_to_image(rect_corners(init + d, heading_deg, L_m, W_m)), dtype=float)
        return np.array([uv[:, 1].max() - tv, (uv[:, 0].min() + uv[:, 0].max()) / 2.0 - tu])

    try:
        r0 = resid(np.zeros(2))
        if not np.isfinite(r0).all():
            return nan2, nan42, False, np.nan
        sol = least_squares(resid, np.zeros(2), method="lm", x_scale=1.0, xtol=1e-12, ftol=1e-12, gtol=1e-12,
                            max_nfev=200)  # fmt: skip
    except (ValueError, FloatingPointError):
        return nan2, nan42, False, np.nan
    r = float(np.max(np.abs(sol.fun)))
    if not np.isfinite(r):
        return nan2, nan42, False, np.nan
    centre = init + sol.x
    return centre, rect_corners(centre, heading_deg, L_m, W_m), bool(r < resid_ok_px), r

        else:

docs.text:
M4: CarFusion wheel keypoints -> body centre and directed heading (ported from the speed study's m4.py; base design section 6.1).

Keypoint schema: 0 right-front, 1 left-front, 2 right-back, 3 left-back; only the same-side pairs right (0, 2) and left (1, 3) are used. Keypoints are distorted pixels (like the bbox); to_ground maps them to world contacts (ground.image_to_world for contact landmarks, hub_to_contact through the camera for hub landmarks, None when hub landmarks meet a camera that failed its consistency check: camera_invalid). Image heights ("lower in the image", the bbox-bottom cue) use the ground contacts re-projected with world_to_image, in the same pixels as the bbox.

Body centre (world) and directed heading from four wheel keypoints [RF, LF, RB, LB] (distorted px).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m4.py 
def solve_m4(kp_uv, box_xywh, psi_ref_deg, cls, dh, to_ground, cfg: FootprintConfig | None = None) -> M4Result:
    """Body centre (world) and directed heading from four wheel keypoints [RF, LF, RB, LB] (distorted px)."""
    cfg = _cfg(cfg)
    if to_ground is None:
        return M4Result(fail_reason="camera_invalid")
    if int(cls) not in cfg.priors_ft:
        return M4Result(fail_reason="no_prior")
    kp_uv = np.asarray(kp_uv, dtype=float).reshape(4, 2)
    psi = float(psi_ref_deg)
    pri = cfg.priors_ft[int(cls)]
    wb_m, tr_m = pri["wheelbase"] * FT, pri["track"] * FT
    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in box_xywh)

    G = np.full((4, 2), np.nan)
    fin = np.isfinite(kp_uv).all(axis=1)
    if fin.any():
        G[fin] = np.asarray(to_ground(kp_uv[fin]), dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    gfin = np.isfinite(G).all(axis=1)
    v_img = np.full(4, np.nan)  # image v of the ground contacts (same pixels as the bbox)
    if gfin.any():
        v_img[gfin] = np.asarray(dh.world_to_image(G[gfin]), dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)[:, 1]

    # 1. Acceptance; the lower passing pair (larger mean v) is chosen.
    passing = [(side, np.mean(v_img[list(ij)])) for side, ij in PAIRS.items()
               if np.isfinite(psi) and _pair_accept(G[ij[0]], G[ij[1]], psi, wb_m, cfg)]  # fmt: skip
    if not passing:
        return M4Result(fail_reason="no_valid_pair")
    side = max(passing, key=lambda t: t[1] if np.isfinite(t[1]) else -np.inf)[0]
    other = "L" if side == "R" else "R"
    (fi, bi), (ofi, obi) = PAIRS[side], PAIRS[other]
    F, B = G[fi], G[bi]
    res = M4Result(pair_side=side, wheelbase_ft=float(np.linalg.norm(F - B) / FT))

    # 2. Front.
    d_front = (F - B) / np.linalg.norm(F - B)
    res.front_flipped = bool(diff_directed(compass_deg(d_front), psi) > 90.0)
    if res.front_flipped:
        d_front = -d_front
    res.d_front = d_front
    n_left = rot_ccw(d_front)
    axle = (F + B) / 2.0

    # 3. Interior side: credible other pair, else camera-away, else ambiguous.
    reject, s = _credibility(G[ofi], G[obi], kp_uv[[ofi, obi]], axle, d_front, n_left, psi, wb_m, tr_m, cfg)
    res.side_reject = reject
    sign = 0.0
    if reject == "":
        sign = float(np.sign(s))
        res.interior_source = "other_pair"
        res.track_ft = abs(s) / FT
    else:
        v_ch, v_ot = v_img[[fi, bi]], v_img[[ofi, obi]]
        depth_ok = (not np.isfinite(v_ot).all()) or bool(v_ch.mean() >= v_ot.mean() + cfg.m4_near_dv_px)
        bottom_ok = bool(np.any(np.abs((y + h) - v_ch) <= cfg.m4_near_bottom_frac * h))  # two-sided (R8)
        if depth_ok and bottom_ok:
            a = away_dir(dh, np.asarray(dh.world_to_image(axle[None, :]), dtype=float))[0]
            dot = float(a @ n_left)
            if np.isfinite(dot) and abs(dot) >= cfg.m4_camera_away_dot:
                sign = float(np.sign(dot))
                res.interior_source = "camera_away"
    if sign == 0.0:
        res.fail_reason = "side_ambiguous"
        return res

    # 4. Centre. 5. Label case: interior +n_left means the pair is physically the vehicle's right side.
    res.centre = axle + (tr_m / 2.0) * sign * n_left + ((pri["front_oh"] - pri["rear_oh"]) * FT / 2.0) * d_front
    geo_side = "R" if sign > 0 else "L"
    res.label_case = _LABEL_CASE[(res.front_flipped, geo_side != side)]
    res.valid = True
    return res

def to_ground_for(ctx, cls):
    """The contact function of a class: the homography for contact landmarks, the camera's hub drop for hubs."""
    cfg = ctx.config
    if cfg.wheel_landmark == "contact":
        return lambda uv: ctx.ground.image_to_world(uv)
    cam = ctx.camera()
    if cam is None:
        return None
    from ...transform.camera import hub_to_contact

    r_m = cfg.priors_ft.get(int(cls), {}).get("wheel_r", np.nan) * FT
    return lambda uv: hub_to_contact(cam, ctx.ground.undistort(uv), r_m)

def front_conflict(track, valid, flipped, min_rows: int, share: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per row: its track has at least `min_rows` native-valid rows and more than `share` of them front-flipped."""
    df = pd.DataFrame({"track": track, "ok": valid, "f": flipped & valid})
    g = df[df["ok"]].groupby("track")["f"].agg(["size", "mean"])
    flag = (g["size"] >= min_rows) & (g["mean"] > share)
    return df["track"].map(flag).fillna(False).to_numpy(dtype=bool)

@register_locator("M4", needs=("keypoints",), aliases="wheel_keypoints")
def locate_m4(rows, ctx) -> LocatorResult:
    """Fail reasons: no_match, no_heading, camera_invalid, no_valid_pair, side_ambiguous, no_prior."""
    cfg = ctx.config
    n = len(rows)
    res = LocatorResult.empty(n, "no_match")
    kp = ctx.tables["keypoints"]
    missing = [c for c in ["track", "frame", *KP_COLUMNS] if c not in kp.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"keypoints table lacks column(s) {missing}")
    hit = kp.drop_duplicates(["track", "frame"]).set_index(["track", "frame"])
    hit = hit.reindex(list(zip(rows["track"].to_numpy(), rows["frame"].to_numpy())))
    kp_arr = hit[KP_COLUMNS].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    present = hit[KP_COLUMNS].notna().any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    boxes = rows[list(cfg.box_cols)].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    psi = rows["ref_heading_deg"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    cls = rows["cls_track"].to_numpy()
    diag = {c: np.full(n, "", dtype=object) for c in ("m4_pair_side", "m4_label_case", "m4_interior_source",
                                                       "m4_side_reject")}  # fmt: skip
    flipped = np.zeros(n, bool)
    wb, tr = np.full(n, np.nan), np.full(n, np.nan)
    grounds: dict = {}
    for i in range(n):
        if not present[i]:
            continue
        if not np.isfinite(psi[i]):
            res.fail_reason[i] = "no_heading"
            continue
        c = int(cls[i])
        if c not in grounds:
            grounds[c] = to_ground_for(ctx, c)
        r = solve_m4(kp_arr[i].reshape(4, 2), boxes[i], psi[i], c, ctx.ground, grounds[c], cfg)
        res.fail_reason[i] = r.fail_reason
        diag["m4_pair_side"][i], diag["m4_label_case"][i] = r.pair_side, r.label_case
        diag["m4_interior_source"][i], diag["m4_side_reject"][i] = r.interior_source, r.side_reject
        flipped[i], wb[i], tr[i] = r.front_flipped, r.wheelbase_ft, r.track_ft
        if r.valid:
            res.ok[i] = True
            res.x[i], res.y[i] = r.centre
            res.orient_deg[i], res.orient_kind[i] = float(compass_deg(r.d_front)), "directed"
    res.extras.update(diag)
    res.extras["m4_front_flipped"] = flipped
    res.extras["m4_wheelbase_ft"], res.extras["m4_track_ft"] = wb, tr
    res.extras["m4_front_conflict"] = front_conflict(rows["track"].to_numpy(), res.ok, flipped,
                                                     cfg.m4_front_conflict_min_rows, cfg.m4_front_conflict_share)  # fmt: skip
    return res

M5: lower mask outline -> nominal-size rectangle fit (ported from the speed study's m5.py; base design section 6).

  • R19: the fit starts from fixed axes 0/45/90/135 deg and never sees psi_ref.
  • R20: a one-sided outline is mirror-ambiguous; after the fit the centre must lie on the away-from-camera side of the outline, else it is reflected across the fitted near side (mirror_away; diagnostic m5_flipped).
  • R23: outline points below the bbox bottom (v > y + h + 1 px) are dropped before fitting. Change from the study: the outline comes from the mask contours of the masks table (one SAM pass serves M5 and M7, design section 15), rasterised with every stored component.

def fit_rect(points_EN, L_m, W_m, init_centre):
    """(centre, axis_deg in [0, 180), resid_ft RMS of boundary distance, sides_covered); fixed starts (R19)."""
    pts = np.asarray(points_EN, dtype=float)
    c0 = np.asarray(init_centre, dtype=float)
    best = None
    for a0 in START_DEG:
        p0 = np.array([c0[0], c0[1], np.radians(a0)])
        sol = least_squares(lambda p: _boundary_dist(pts, p, L_m, W_m), p0, method="lm", xtol=1e-10, ftol=1e-10,
                            max_nfev=400)  # fmt: skip
        if best is None or sol.cost < best.cost:
            best = sol
    c = best.x[:2]
    th = best.x[2]
    return (c, float(to_undirected(np.degrees(th))), *_resid_sides(pts, c, th, L_m, W_m))

docs.text:
mirror_away(
    pts, centre, axis_deg, L_m, W_m, away
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]

(centre, flipped): unchanged when (centre - outline mean) . away > 0, else reflected across the rectangle side closest to the outline points (R20).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m5.py 
def mirror_away(pts, centre, axis_deg, L_m, W_m, away) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]:
    """(centre, flipped): unchanged when (centre - outline mean) . away > 0, else reflected across the rectangle side
    closest to the outline points (R20)."""
    pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=float)
    c = np.asarray(centre, dtype=float)
    if float((c - pts.mean(axis=0)) @ np.asarray(away, dtype=float)) > 0:
        return c, False
    th = np.radians(axis_deg)
    t = np.array([np.sin(th), np.cos(th)])
    s = np.array([-t[1], t[0]])
    best, offset = np.inf, None
    for normal, h, along, ha in ((s, W_m / 2.0, t, L_m / 2.0), (t, L_m / 2.0, s, W_m / 2.0)):
        for sign in (1.0, -1.0):
            off = sign * h * normal  # centre -> side midpoint
            d = pts - (c + off)
            a = np.clip(d @ along, -ha, ha)
            dist = float(np.mean(np.linalg.norm(d - a[:, None] * along, axis=1)))
            if dist < best:
                best, offset = dist, off
    return c + 2.0 * offset, True

def solve_m5(outline_px, box_xywh, ground, L_m, W_m, init, min_cols: int = 8, max_resid_ft: float = 1.0) -> dict:
    """One row: outline pixels -> dict(ok, reason, centre, axis, cols, resid_ft, sides, flipped)."""
    out = dict(ok=False, reason="", centre=np.full(2, np.nan), axis=np.nan, cols=0, resid_ft=np.nan, sides=0,
               flipped=False)  # fmt: skip
    if outline_px is None:
        out["reason"] = "no_match"
        return out
    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in box_xywh)
    o = np.asarray(outline_px, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    o = o[~(o[:, 1] > y + h + BELOW_BOTTOM_PX)]  # R23
    out["cols"] = len(o)
    if len(o) < min_cols:
        out["reason"] = "few_columns"
        return out
    pts = project(ground, o)
    try:
        c, ax, r, s = fit_rect(pts, L_m, W_m, init)
        c, flipped = mirror_away(pts, c, ax, L_m, W_m, away_dir(ground, o.mean(axis=0))[0])
        if flipped:
            r, s = _resid_sides(pts, c, np.radians(ax), L_m, W_m)
    except (ValueError, FloatingPointError):
        out["reason"] = "fit_residual"
        return out
    out.update(resid_ft=r, sides=s, flipped=flipped)
    if not np.isfinite(r) or r > max_resid_ft:
        out["reason"] = "fit_residual"
        return out
    out.update(ok=True, centre=c, axis=ax)
    return out

@register_locator("M6", needs=("cuboids",), aliases="cuboid")
def locate_m6(rows, ctx) -> LocatorResult:
    """Fail reasons: no_match (no row, IoU below m6_min_iou, non-finite corners); implausible_size (length or width
    below m6_size_gate of the class's nominal size: a collapsed face)."""
    cfg = ctx.config
    n = len(rows)
    res = LocatorResult.empty(n, "no_match")
    cub = ctx.tables["cuboids"]
    missing = [c for c in ["track", "frame", *UV_COLS] if c not in cub.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"cuboids table lacks column(s) {missing}")
    cub = cub.drop_duplicates(["track", "frame"]).set_index(["track", "frame"])
    hit = cub.reindex(list(zip(rows["track"].to_numpy(), rows["frame"].to_numpy())))
    uv = hit[UV_COLS].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    iou = hit["iou"].to_numpy(dtype=float) if "iou" in hit.columns else np.where(np.isfinite(uv).all(1), 1.0, np.nan)
    cls = rows["cls_track"].to_numpy()
    raw = np.full((n, 8), np.nan)
    for i in range(n):
        if not (iou[i] >= cfg.m6_min_iou) or not np.isfinite(uv[i]).all():
            continue
        corners, cen, L, W, axis = face_geometry(uv[i].reshape(4, 2), ctx.ground)
        nom_l, nom_w = cfg.size_of(cls[i])
        if L < cfg.m6_size_gate * nom_l * FT or W < cfg.m6_size_gate * nom_w * FT:
            res.fail_reason[i] = "implausible_size"
            continue
        res.ok[i], res.fail_reason[i] = True, ""
        res.x[i], res.y[i] = cen
        res.orient_deg[i], res.orient_kind[i] = axis, "axis"
        res.len_ft[i], res.wid_ft[i] = L / FT, W / FT
        raw[i] = corners.ravel()
    res.extras.update({c: raw[:, j] for j, c in enumerate(RAW_COLS)})
    res.extras["m6_len_ft"], res.extras["m6_wid_ft"] = res.len_ft.copy(), res.wid_ft.copy()
    res.extras["m6_iou"] = np.where(res.ok, iou, np.nan)
    return res

docs.title: m7
docs.text:
M7: wheel-anchored rigid-body fit per bus or truck segment (M7 design rev 7 plus the M7 notes' decisions to 2026-11-10; footprint design section 7.6). Ported from the speed study's m7.py, m7_candidates.py and the job, cache and table parts of m7_runner.py (snapshot docs/study-snapshot-2026-11-10.json).

Per segment of a cls 5/7 track: frozen observations from the mask contours (frame_obs_from_mask, the other boxes of each frame from the full track table), an initial pose from the M2 points and psi_ref, solve_track, then rows: wheels2 / wheel_front / wheel_rear / silhouette rows are native; kinematic rows carry the solve's pose and centre covariance for admission (design 7.7); a failed solve fails every row with its gate reason. Solves run in workers spawned processes (one BLAS thread each) and are cached under <cache_dir>/m7solve/.

def init_pose(m2_local: np.ndarray, psi: np.ndarray):
    """Initial centre (M2 points interpolated across rows without one) and heading (psi_ref interpolated; else the
    path direction), study m7_runner._init_pose. None when no row has an M2 point."""
    ok = np.isfinite(m2_local).all(axis=1)
    if not ok.any():
        return None
    c = m2_local.copy()
    c[~ok] = np.nan
    c0 = pd.DataFrame(c).interpolate(limit_direction="both").to_numpy(float)
    p = _interp_angle(psi)
    if not np.isfinite(p).all():
        d = np.gradient(c0, axis=0) if len(c0) > 1 else np.array([[0.0, 1.0]])
        p = np.degrees(np.arctan2(d[:, 0], d[:, 1])) % 360
    return c0, p

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m7/__init__.py 
def job_key(tr, ns: dict, camera_ok: bool, ident) -> str:
    """Hash of the solve's inputs: code, settings, identity, frames, initial pose, camera and frozen observations."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    h.update(code_version().encode())
    h.update(json.dumps(ns, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode())
    h.update(json.dumps([*ident, bool(camera_ok)], default=str).encode())
    _upd(h, tr.frames)
    for a in (tr.origin, tr.init_centre, tr.init_psi_deg, [tr.cls, tr.dt]):
        _upd(h, np.asarray(a, float))
    for k, v in sorted(vars(tr.cam).items()):
        h.update(k.encode())
        _upd(h, np.asarray(v, float)) if np.asarray(v).dtype.kind in "biuf" else h.update(repr(v).encode())
    for o in tr.obs:
        _upd(h, [o.frame])
        for a in (o.cand, o.kappa, o.env_u, o.env_v, o.ext, o.cand_s):
            _upd(h, np.asarray(a, float))
    return h.hexdigest()

def solve_one(tr, ns: dict, camera_ok: bool = True) -> dict:
    """One solve -> {"frames", "summary", "seconds"} or {"error", "traceback", "seconds"}. Never raises."""
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        with using(ns):
            res = m7.solve_track(tr, camera_ok=camera_ok)
        out = {"frames": res["frames"], "summary": res["summary"]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad segment must not lose the run; it is reported
        out = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}", "traceback": traceback.format_exc()}
    out["seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return out

def solve_jobs(jobs: list[dict], ns: dict, cache_dir=None, workers: int = 1, camera_ok: bool = True) -> dict:
    """{key: result}: cached results reused; the rest solved longest first, in `workers` spawned processes."""
    out, todo = {}, []
    for j in jobs:
        p = _cache_path(cache_dir, j["key"]) if cache_dir is not None else None
        if p is not None and p.is_file():
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                out[j["key"]] = {**pickle.load(f), "cached": True}
        elif j["key"] not in {t["key"] for t in todo}:
            todo.append(j)
    todo.sort(key=lambda j: -len(j["tr"].frames))

    def done(j, r):
        out[j["key"]] = {**r, "cached": False}
        if cache_dir is not None and "error" not in r:
            _save(_cache_path(cache_dir, j["key"]), r)

    if workers <= 1 or len(todo) <= 1:
        for j in todo:
            done(j, solve_one(j["tr"], ns, camera_ok))
        return out
    saved = {k: os.environ.get(k) for k in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS")}
    os.environ.update({k: "1" for k in saved})  # spawned children read these when they import numpy
    try:
        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(workers, len(todo)), mp_context=get_context("spawn")) as ex:
            fut = {ex.submit(solve_one, j["tr"], ns, camera_ok): j for j in todo}
            for f in as_completed(fut):
                done(fut[f], f.result())
    finally:
        for k, v in saved.items():
            if v is None:
                os.environ.pop(k, None)
            else:
                os.environ[k] = v
    return out

docs.text:
locate_m7(rows: DataFrame, ctx) -> LocatorResult

See the module docstring. Fail reasons: the solve's gate reason, camera_invalid, too_few_frames, no_initial_pose, solve_error; kinematic rows of a passed solve are supplied with support "kinematic".

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m7/__init__.py 
@register_locator("M7", needs=("masks",), scope="segment", classes=(5, 7), aliases="wheel_fit")
def locate_m7(rows: pd.DataFrame, ctx) -> LocatorResult:
    """See the module docstring. Fail reasons: the solve's gate reason, camera_invalid, too_few_frames,
    no_initial_pose, solve_error; kinematic rows of a passed solve are supplied with support "kinematic"."""
    cfg = ctx.config
    n = len(rows)
    res = LocatorResult.empty(n)
    ex = {k: np.full(n, np.nan) for k in ("m7_x", "m7_y", "m7_psi_deg", "m7_n_inliers", "m7_n_outliers",
                                           "m7_sd_along_ft", "m7_sd_across_ft", "m7_sd_heading_deg",
                                           "m7_cov_centre_ee", "m7_cov_centre_en", "m7_cov_centre_nn")}  # fmt: skip
    obj = {k: np.full(n, "", dtype=object) for k in ("m7_support", "m7_near_side", "m7_fail_reason")}
    solve_ok = np.zeros(n, bool)
    per: dict = {}
    res.seg_len_ft, res.seg_wid_ft = np.full(n, np.nan), np.full(n, np.nan)
    res.seg_dims_source = np.full(n, "", dtype=object)
    res.cov = np.full((n, 2, 2), np.nan)
    cam = ctx.camera()
    origin = np.asarray(ctx.origin, float)
    ns = _ns(ctx)
    by_frame = {int(f): g for f, g in ctx.all_boxes.groupby("frame")}
    groups = [np.asarray(v) for v in rows.groupby(["track", "seg"], sort=True).indices.values()]
    jobs, reason = [], {}
    for g in groups:
        sub = rows.iloc[g]
        frames = sub["frame"].to_numpy(int)
        ident = (int(sub["track"].iloc[0]), int(sub["seg"].iloc[0]), int(sub["cls_track"].iloc[0]))
        if cam is None:
            reason[id(g)] = "camera_invalid"
            continue
        if len(frames) > 1 and not (np.diff(frames) == 1).all():
            raise ValueError(f"M7: segment {ident[:2]} does not have consecutive frames")
        if len(frames) < ns["M7_MIN_SUPPORT_FRAMES"]:
            reason[id(g)] = "too_few_frames"
            continue
        m2 = sub[["m2_x", "m2_y"]].to_numpy(float) - origin
        init = init_pose(m2, sub["ref_heading_deg"].to_numpy(float))
        if init is None:
            reason[id(g)] = "no_initial_pose"
            continue
        tr = m7.Track(frames, _obs(sub, ctx, cam, by_frame), cam, origin, init[0], init[1], ident[2], 1.0 / cfg.fps)
        jobs.append({"g": g, "tr": tr, "ident": ident, "key": job_key(tr, ns, True, ident)})
    results = solve_jobs(jobs, ns, ctx.cache_dir, ctx.workers, True)
    solves = []
    for g in groups:
        if id(g) in reason:
            res.fail_reason[g] = reason[id(g)]
            obj["m7_fail_reason"][g] = reason[id(g)]
    for j in jobs:
        g, r = j["g"], results[j["key"]]
        if "error" in r:
            res.fail_reason[g] = "solve_error"
            obj["m7_fail_reason"][g] = "solve_error"
            solves.append({"track": j["ident"][0], "seg": j["ident"][1], "fail_reason": "solve_error",
                           "error": r["error"], "seconds": r.get("seconds", np.nan)})  # fmt: skip
            continue
        sm, fr = r["summary"], r["frames"].reset_index(drop=True)
        fail = sm["fail_reason"]
        passed = fail == ""
        solves.append({"track": j["ident"][0], "seg": j["ident"][1], "cls": j["ident"][2], "n_frames": len(g),
                       "seconds": r.get("seconds", np.nan), "cached": r.get("cached", False),
                       **{k: (json.dumps(v, default=float) if isinstance(v, dict) else v) for k, v in sm.items()}})  # fmt: skip
        pos = fr.set_index("frame").reindex(rows["frame"].to_numpy()[g])
        cen = pos[["e_nat", "n_nat"]].to_numpy(float) + origin
        sup = pos["m7_support"].fillna("").to_numpy(dtype=object)
        cov = pos[["m7_cov_centre_ee", "m7_cov_centre_en", "m7_cov_centre_en", "m7_cov_centre_nn"]].to_numpy(float)
        ex["m7_x"][g], ex["m7_y"][g], ex["m7_psi_deg"][g] = cen[:, 0], cen[:, 1], pos["psi_deg"].to_numpy(float)
        for k in ("m7_n_inliers", "m7_n_outliers", "m7_sd_along_ft", "m7_sd_across_ft", "m7_sd_heading_deg",
                  "m7_cov_centre_ee", "m7_cov_centre_en", "m7_cov_centre_nn"):
            ex[k][g] = pos[k].to_numpy(float)
        obj["m7_support"][g], obj["m7_near_side"][g] = sup, pos["near_side"].astype(object).to_numpy()
        obj["m7_fail_reason"][g] = fail
        solve_ok[g] = passed
        for k, v in _summary_extras(sm).items():
            per.setdefault(k, np.full(n, np.nan if isinstance(v, float) else "", dtype=float if isinstance(v, float) else object))
            per[k][g] = v
        if not passed:
            res.fail_reason[g] = fail
            continue
        res.seg_len_ft[g], res.seg_wid_ft[g] = sm["length_ft"], sm["width_ft"]
        res.seg_dims_source[g] = sm.get("dims_source", "m7_measured")
        native = np.isin(sup, NATIVE_SUPPORT)
        kin = sup == "kinematic"
        ok = (native | kin) & np.isfinite(cen).all(axis=1)
        res.ok[g] = ok
        res.fail_reason[g] = np.where(ok, "", "no_observation")
        res.x[g], res.y[g] = cen[:, 0], cen[:, 1]
        res.orient_deg[g], res.orient_kind[g] = pos["psi_deg"].to_numpy(float), "directed"
        res.support[g] = np.where(kin, "kinematic", "native").astype(object)
        R = cov.reshape(-1, 2, 2) * cfg.kin_meas_scale**2 + (cfg.kin_sd_floor_ft * FT) ** 2 * np.eye(2)
        res.cov[g] = np.where(kin[:, None, None], R, np.nan)
    res.extras.update(ex)
    res.extras.update(obj)
    res.extras.update(per)
    res.extras["m7_solve_ok"] = solve_ok
    ctx.info.setdefault("m7_solves", []).extend(solves)
    return res

Changes: settings through the per-solve namespace S; image-size and edge defaults resolved at call time; rasterising and the lower outline from tssa.footprint.masks (OpenCV imported on first use).

M7 wheel-contact candidates from a SAM mask, without a pose (design 2026-11-08-m7, section 5.1).

Per row: lower outline of the mask inside the bbox -> drop untrustworthy columns (image edge, nearer boxes, leaks below the bbox) -> undistort -> robust one- or two-segment body line (points below it are down-weighted, so tyre bumps do not pull it) -> runs of columns protruding below the line -> runs split at dips -> tyre-size check against the expected tyre diameter D_c at the run's own ground point -> candidate = the run's lowest pixel, with its frozen gate g_c and rejection price kappa_c.

Geometry inputs: - dh: ground model (image_to_world on DISTORTED pixels, undistort); - cam: camera.Camera (project UTM 3-D -> UNDISTORTED pixels). Contours are lists of (k, 2) distorted pixel polygons (several components allowed).

def rho(z):

def split_contours(arr) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """(n, 2) array with NaN separator rows -> list of polygons (the m7 cache format)."""
    arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    out, cur = [], []
    for p in arr:
        if np.isnan(p).any():
            if cur:
                out.append(np.array(cur))
            cur = []
        else:
            cur.append(p)
    if cur:
        out.append(np.array(cur))
    return out

def join_contours(polys) -> np.ndarray:
    """List of polygons -> (n, 2) with a NaN row after each polygon."""

        parts.append(np.asarray(p, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2))

Columns of outline (distorted px) that are boundary evidence: not at the image edge, not inside a nearer box of the same frame (other_boxes rows x, y, w, h with a lower bottom edge), not leaking below the bbox.

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m7/candidates.py 
def trusted_mask(outline, box, other_boxes, img_size=None, edge_px=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Columns of `outline` (distorted px) that are boundary evidence: not at the image edge, not inside a nearer
    box of the same frame (`other_boxes` rows x, y, w, h with a lower bottom edge), not leaking below the bbox."""
    img_size = S.IMG_SIZE if img_size is None else img_size
    edge_px = S.EDGE_PX if edge_px is None else edge_px
    o = np.asarray(outline, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    W, H = img_size
    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in box)
    ok = (o[:, 0] >= edge_px) & (o[:, 0] <= W - 1 - edge_px) & (o[:, 1] <= H - 1 - edge_px)
    ok &= o[:, 1] <= y + h + BELOW_BOTTOM_PX
    for ox, oy, ow, oh in np.asarray(other_boxes, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 4):
        if oy + oh <= y + h:  # not nearer than this vehicle
            continue
        inside = (o[:, 0] >= ox) & (o[:, 0] <= ox + ow) & (o[:, 1] >= oy) & (o[:, 1] <= oy + oh)
        ok &= ~inside
    return ok

body_line(uv, thr)

Robust one- or two-segment (continuous hinge) body line through undistorted outline points.

Returns (v_line at each point, info dict: segments, break_u, cost).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m7/candidates.py 
def body_line(uv, thr):
    """Robust one- or two-segment (continuous hinge) body line through undistorted outline points.

    Returns (v_line at each point, info dict: segments, break_u, cost)."""
    u, v = uv[:, 0], uv[:, 1]
    one = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(u), u])
    _, r1, c1 = _irls_line(u, v, one, thr)
    best = (c1, v - r1, {"segments": 1, "break_u": np.nan, "cost": c1})
    n = len(u)
    for q in np.linspace(5, 85, N_BREAKS):
        b = np.percentile(u, q)
        left = (u <= b).sum()
        if min(left, n - left) < max(0.15 * n, 4):
            continue
        two = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(u), u, np.maximum(0.0, u - b)])
        _, r2, c2 = _irls_line(u, v, two, thr)
        if c2 < best[0] and c2 < S.M7_TWO_SEG_GAIN * c1:
            best = (c2, v - r2, {"segments": 2, "break_u": float(b), "cost": c2})
    return best[1], best[2]

docs.text:
tyre_px(dh, cam, uv_dist, r_ft) -> np.ndarray

Expected tyre diameter in undistorted px at each distorted pixel's own ground point (no pose).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/locators/m7/candidates.py 
def tyre_px(dh, cam, uv_dist, r_ft) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expected tyre diameter in undistorted px at each distorted pixel's own ground point (no pose)."""
    uv = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(uv_dist, dtype=float))
    G = np.asarray(dh.image_to_world(uv), dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    z = 2.0 * r_ft * S.FT
    p0 = cam.project(np.column_stack([G, np.zeros(len(G))]))
    p1 = cam.project(np.column_stack([G, np.full(len(G), z)]))
    return np.linalg.norm(p1 - p0, axis=1)

def extract(contours, box, other_boxes, dh, cam, cls, img_size=None):
    """Candidates of one row and a summary dict. `contours`: list of distorted pixel polygons."""
    summary = {"n_cols": 0, "n_trusted": 0, "segments": 0, "break_u": np.nan, "n_runs": 0, "n_cand": 0,
               "reason": ""}  # fmt: skip
    empty = pd.DataFrame(columns=CAND_COLUMNS)
    if not contours:
        summary["reason"] = "no_mask"
        return empty, summary, None
    mask = rasterise(contours, img_size)
    o = lower_outline(mask, box)
    summary["n_cols"] = len(o)
    ok = trusted_mask(o, box, other_boxes, img_size)
    o = o[ok]
    summary["n_trusted"] = len(o)
    if len(o) < S.M7_MIN_OUTLINE_COLS:
        summary["reason"] = "few_columns"
        return empty, summary, None
    cols = np.round(o[:, 0]).astype(int)
    uv = np.asarray(dh.undistort(o), dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    h = float(box[3])
    thr = S.M7_PROTRUDE_PX * h / 100.0
    v_line, info = body_line(uv, thr)
    summary.update(segments=info["segments"], break_u=info["break_u"])
    depth = uv[:, 1] - v_line
    r_ft = S.M7_WHEEL_R_REF_FT[int(cls)]
    recs = []
    runs = [s for run in _runs(depth > thr, cols) for s in _split_at_dips(run, depth, thr)]
    summary["n_runs"] = len(runs)
    for run in runs:
        bottom = run[uv[run, 1] >= uv[run, 1].max() - 0.75]  # a raster bottom is flat: take its middle
        k = bottom[len(bottom) // 2]
        pu, pv = float(o[bottom, 0].mean()), float(o[k, 1])
        pu_und = float(uv[bottom, 0].mean())
        D = float(tyre_px(dh, cam, np.array([pu, pv]), r_ft)[0])
        width = float(uv[run[-1], 0] - uv[run[0], 0] + 1.0)
        ratio = width / D if D > 0 else np.nan
        ok_w = S.M7_TYRE_W_MIN <= ratio <= S.M7_TYRE_W_MAX
        reject = "" if ok_w else ("narrow" if ratio < S.M7_TYRE_W_MIN else "wide")
        if not reject and depth[k] > S.M7_MAX_DEPTH_TYRES * D:
            ok_w, reject = False, "deep"
        gate = max(S.M7_GATE_MIN_PX, S.M7_GATE_TYRES * D)
        recs.append([len(recs), pu, pv, pu_und, uv[k, 1], float(depth[k]), width, D, ratio, gate,
                     float(rho(gate / S.M7_SIGMA_WHEEL_PX)), bool(ok_w), reject])  # fmt: skip
    cand = pd.DataFrame(recs, columns=CAND_COLUMNS)
    cand = _dedupe(cand)
    summary["n_cand"] = int(cand["accepted"].sum()) if len(cand) else 0
    debug = {"outline": o, "uv": uv, "v_line": v_line, "depth": depth, "thr": thr, "dropped": None}
    return cand, summary, debug

docs.title: solver
docs.text:
Ported from the speed study's m7.py (sha256 d8fc196b1e8375caeaef486eaadcc7314bbf65eaa82c92b26ed67ef8bcbf108f, snapshot docs/study-snapshot-2026-11-10.json). Changes: settings through the per-solve namespace S (an M7Config plus FT, MPS_TO_MPH, IMG_SIZE, EDGE_PX, SIZE_FT) instead of the study's settings module; image-size default resolved at call time; the width-hold decision moved into width_held (same expression) so it can be tested on its own. Speed (2026-11-11, results bit-identical): the sparsity pattern is built with numpy, the matched candidates are packed once per association, and the finite-difference Jacobian is _FDJac (scipy's 2-point sparse scheme with the column groups known in advance) instead of scipy's own, which re-sliced the pattern on every call.

M7: wheel-anchored rigid-body fit of one bus or truck segment (design 2026-11-08-m7, rev 5, sections 4-8).

Frames and units: positions are LOCAL metres (the grid's frame; origin converts to UTM for the camera), headings compass radians internally (0 = north, clockwise), f = (sin psi, cos psi), n_left = (-cos psi, sin psi). Image residuals are in UNDISTORTED pixels (cam.project).

Unknowns: per frame the rear-axle centre R_k (2) and heading psi_k; per solve the statics theta = (L_w, L_f, L_r, W, H[, s_t]) in metres. Observations per frame (FrameObs, frozen before any fit): wheel candidates with frozen rejection prices kappa_c, lower-envelope columns and the two end extents.

Objective F (section 7.4) = sum over candidates of [matched: rho(|d| / sigma_t) | rejected: kappa_c] + envelope and extent rho terms + 1/2 motion z^2 + 1/2 prior z^2, rho(z) = log(1 + z^2). Association (5.2) is the exact minimiser of F's wheel part for a pose; the pose is fitted by IRLS (a majorise-minimise step for Cauchy) with backtracking on F. The evidence score E (Laplace over the statics) is computed once per completed fit and only compares models (axle configuration, subtype).

@classmethod
def load_npz(cls, path) -> "MaskTable":
    """Read the layout `save_npz` writes (also the speed study's m7 cache `outlines.npz`)."""
    z = np.load(path, allow_pickle=False)
    track, frame, count, pts = z["track"], z["frame"], z["count"], z["pts"]  # each array read once
    ends = np.cumsum(count)
    starts = ends - count
    data = {(t, f): split_contours(pts[a:b]) for t, f, a, b in zip(track, frame, starts, ends)}
    outl = {}
    if "o_pts" in z.files:
        ot, of, oc, op = z["o_track"], z["o_frame"], z["o_count"], z["o_pts"]
        oe = np.cumsum(oc)
        outl = {(t, f): op[a:b] for t, f, a, b in zip(ot, of, oe - oc, oe)}
    return cls(data, outl)

def split_contours(arr) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """(n, 2) array with NaN separator rows -> list of polygons."""
    arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
    if not len(arr):
        return []
    sep = np.isnan(arr).any(axis=1)
    out, start = [], 0
    for k in np.flatnonzero(sep):
        if k > start:
            out.append(arr[start:k].copy())
        start = k + 1
    if start < len(arr):
        out.append(arr[start:].copy())
    return out

def join_contours(polys) -> np.ndarray:
    """List of polygons -> (n, 2) with a NaN row after each polygon."""
    parts = []
    for p in polys:
        parts.append(np.asarray(p, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2))
        parts.append(np.full((1, 2), np.nan))
    return np.vstack(parts) if parts else np.empty((0, 2))

def rasterise(polys, img_size) -> np.ndarray:
    """Bool (H, W) mask of the filled polygons."""
    cv2 = _cv2()
    W, H = (int(round(v)) for v in img_size)
    canvas = np.zeros((H, W), np.uint8)
    pts = [np.round(np.asarray(p)).astype(np.int32) for p in polys if len(p) >= 3]
    if pts:
        cv2.fillPoly(canvas, pts, 1)
    return canvas.astype(bool)

docs.text:
component_areas(polys) -> np.ndarray

Area + perimeter samples of each contour polygon (the study's cv2.contourArea(c) + len(c), by the shoelace formula, so thin parts still count).

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/masks.py 
def component_areas(polys) -> np.ndarray:
    """Area + perimeter samples of each contour polygon (the study's `cv2.contourArea(c) + len(c)`, by the
    shoelace formula, so thin parts still count)."""
    out = []
    for p in polys:
        p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)
        x, y = p[:, 0], p[:, 1]
        out.append(0.5 * abs(float(np.dot(x, np.roll(y, -1)) - np.dot(y, np.roll(x, -1)))) + len(p))
    return np.asarray(out, dtype=float)

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/masks.py 
def keep_components(polys, frac: float) -> list:
    """Components holding at least `frac` of the summed area, largest first (study infer.mask_contours); applying it
    again with the same `frac` keeps them all."""
    polys = list(polys)
    if not polys:
        return []
    a = component_areas(polys)
    return [polys[i] for i in np.argsort(-a) if a[i] >= frac * a.sum()]

docs.text:
lower_outline(mask, box_xywh) -> np.ndarray

(m, 2) pixels [u, v]: the largest set row per integer column inside the bbox.

mask is a polygon (k, 2) of pixel vertices, a list of polygons, or an (H, W) bool array.

Source code in src/tssa/footprint/masks.py 
def lower_outline(mask, box_xywh) -> np.ndarray:
    """(m, 2) pixels [u, v]: the largest set row per integer column inside the bbox.

    `mask` is a polygon (k, 2) of pixel vertices, a list of polygons, or an (H, W) bool array.
    """
    x, y, w, h = (float(v) for v in box_xywh)
    if isinstance(mask, (list, tuple)):
        polys = [np.asarray(p, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2) for p in mask]
        if not polys:
            return np.empty((0, 2))
        hi = np.vstack(polys).max(axis=0)
        m = rasterise(polys, (max(hi[0], x + w) + 2, max(hi[1], y + h) + 2))
    else:
        m = np.asarray(mask)
        if m.ndim == 2 and m.shape[1] == 2 and m.dtype != bool:
            if len(m) < 3:
                return np.empty((0, 2))
            m = rasterise([m], (int(np.ceil(max(m[:, 0].max(), x + w))) + 2, int(np.ceil(max(m[:, 1].max(), y + h))) + 2))
    H, Wd = m.shape
    u0, u1 = max(int(np.ceil(x)), 0), min(int(np.floor(x + w)), Wd - 1)
    out = []
    for u in range(u0, u1 + 1):
        rows = np.flatnonzero(m[:, u])
        if len(rows):
            out.append((float(u), float(rows[-1])))
    return np.array(out, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 2)

def __init__(self, homography, config: FootprintConfig | None = None, image_size=None, zone=None, camera=None,
             smoother: TrackSmoother | None = None, speed: SpeedCalculator | None = None, workers: int = 1,
             cache_dir=None, **config_overrides) -> None:  # fmt: skip
    self.config = (config or FootprintConfig()).with_overrides(**config_overrides)
    cfg = self.config
    self.ground = GroundModel.wrap(homography, image_size)
    self.zone = zone
    self._camera = camera
    self._camera_done = camera is not None
    self.smoother = smoother or TrackSmoother(
        "rts", params={"q": cfg.rts_q}, xy_cols=XY, cov_cols=COV, fps=cfg.fps, split_speed=cfg.split_speed_mps,
        fill_max_gap=cfg.fill_max_gap, gap_max_speed=cfg.gap_max_speed_mph / MPS_TO_MPH,
    )  # fmt: skip
    sc = self.smoother.config
    if tuple(sc.xy_cols) != XY or tuple(sc.cov_cols or ()) != COV:
        raise ValueError(f"the smoother must use xy_cols={XY} and cov_cols={COV} (design 7.9: the printer writes the "
                         "final covariance; a sigma column would be inflated twice)")  # fmt: skip
    self.speed = speed or SpeedCalculator(fps=cfg.fps, xy_cols=SMOOTH_XY)
    if tuple(self.speed.xy_cols) != SMOOTH_XY:
        raise ValueError(f"the speed calculator must use xy_cols={SMOOTH_XY}")
    try:  # aliases resolve to the canonical names here, so everything downstream sees M1-M7 (design 16, Q7)
        chains = {c: _canonical_chain(ch) for c, ch in cfg.chains.items()}
        default_chain = _canonical_chain(cfg.default_chain)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"a class chain names an unregistered locator: {exc}") from None
    if chains != {c: tuple(ch) for c, ch in cfg.chains.items()} or default_chain != tuple(cfg.default_chain):
        self.config = cfg = cfg.with_overrides(chains=chains, default_chain=default_chain)
    self.workers = int(workers)
    self.cache_dir = cache_dir
    self.local_origin = None  # world offset of the local frame M7 solves in; None = floor of the M1 minimum
    self.info: dict = {}

def camera(self):
    """The fitted camera, or None when there is no zone or it fails its consistency check (design 8)."""
    if self._camera_done:
        return self._camera
    from ..transform.camera import PinholeCamera, consistency

    self._camera_done = True
    cfg = self.config
    if self.zone is None:
        self.info["camera"] = {"ok": False, "reason": "no zone"}
        return None
    cam = PinholeCamera.fit(self.ground, self.zone, free_principal=cfg.camera_free_principal,
                            pp_prior=cfg.camera_pp_prior)  # fmt: skip
    res = consistency(cam, self.ground, self.zone, cfg.camera_rms_px, cfg.camera_max_px)
    self.info["camera"] = {"f": cam.f, "cx": cam.cx, "cy": cam.cy, "height_m": cam.height, **res}
    self._camera = cam if res["ok"] else None
    return self._camera

def compare(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame, methods=("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5", "M6", "M7"), fallback="M2",
            admit_kinematic=None, only_tracks=None, **tables) -> pd.DataFrame:  # fmt: skip
    """Each method alone on the same grid and reference heading; one long table with a `method` column.

    fallback None: native-only (M7 admission off; admit_kinematic=True raises). fallback set: end-to-end,
    admission from admit_kinematic or the config. Rows a method does not serve are `<method>:class_ineligible`
    and get no fallback. Every input row appears once per method (design 11.2).
    """
    if fallback is None and admit_kinematic is True:
        raise ValueError("admit_kinematic=True contradicts a native-only comparison (fallback=None)")
    admit = False if fallback is None else (self.config.admit_kinematic if admit_kinematic is None
                                            else bool(admit_kinematic))  # fmt: skip
    methods = _canonical_chain(methods)  # aliases accepted; `method` carries the canonical name
    fallback = canonical(fallback) if fallback else fallback
    base = self._prepare(tracks, only_tracks, self._needs_heading({0: tuple(methods)}, ()))
    classes = np.unique(base["cls_track"].dropna())
    parts = []
    for m in methods:
        chain = (m,) if not fallback or fallback == m else (m, fallback)
        loc = self._run_chains(base, {c: chain for c in classes}, admit, tables, stop_on_ineligible=True)
        parts.append(self._finish(loc).assign(method=m))
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

def required_rows(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame, only_tracks=None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per detection table, the rows (track, frame, box) of tracks whose class chain needs it (design 6.4)."""
    df = self._input(tracks)
    cls = _cls_track(df, self.config.cls_col)
    keep = df["track"].isin(only_tracks) if only_tracks is not None else np.ones(len(df), bool)
    out: dict[str, list] = {}
    for c in np.unique(cls.dropna()):
        for name in self.config.chain_of(c):
            for t in REGISTRY[name].needs:
                out.setdefault(t, []).append(df[(cls == c).to_numpy() & np.asarray(keep)])
    cols = ["track", "frame", *self.config.box_cols]
    return {t: pd.concat(v).drop_duplicates(["track", "frame"])[cols].reset_index(drop=True) for t, v in out.items()}

@staticmethod
def to_geodataframe(table: pd.DataFrame, crs=None):
    """One shapely polygon per row (empty where the corners are NaN)."""
    import geopandas as gpd
    from shapely.geometry import Polygon

    c = table[CORNERS].to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 4, 2)
    geoms = [Polygon(q) if np.isfinite(q).all() else Polygon() for q in c]
    return gpd.GeoDataFrame(table.copy(), geometry=geoms, crs=crs)

docs.title: Smoothing (tssa.smooth)
docs.text:
TrackSmoother smooths ground trajectories that are already in metres. It splits tracks where they jump (an implied speed above split_speed), fills short gaps, and smooths each segment with a method chosen by name:

Name Kind Notes ma moving average centred sg5, sg7 median filter + Savitzky-Golay window 5 or 7; method="sg", params={"win": 9} for others rts constant-velocity Kalman filter + RTS smoother uses per-row sigma or covariance when given 
from tssa.smooth import TrackSmoother

sm = TrackSmoother(method="rts", fps=10, xy_cols=("x", "y"))
out = sm.smooth(tracks)                        # adds seg, fill_reason, x_smooth, y_smooth, fallback
side_by_side = sm.compare(tracks)              # every preset on one segmentation

To segment once and smooth many times, call segment() and then smooth(..., segmented=True). VehFootPrinter.estimate() works this way. Speeds are not computed here: pass the smoothed positions to SpeedCalculator.

New kinds are added with register_method, and named presets with register_preset.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
Settings of the track smoothing pipeline (segmentation, gap fill, column names).

Inputs: keyword overrides of the defaults below. Outputs: SmoothConfig, the single source of these settings; a TrackSmoother holds one instance, so two smoothers with different settings can coexist.

docs.title: SmoothConfig dataclass
docs.text:
SmoothConfig(
    fps: float = 10.0,
    xy_cols: tuple = ("x", "y"),
    sigma_col: str | None = None,
    cov_cols: tuple | None = None,
    split_speed: float = 6.0,
    fill_gaps: bool = True,
    fill_max_gap: int = 20,
    gap_max_speed: float = 3.0,
)

Pipeline settings. Positions are in metres (a projected ground plane); a track is split where it jumps.

fps: frames per second of the tracks. xy_cols: names of the input position columns (metres); the smoothed positions keep these names. sigma_col: optional column of the per-row position std-dev in metres; overrides the rts sigma row by row. cov_cols: optional names of three per-row covariance columns (xx, xy, yy) in m^2. Where all three are finite the rts kind uses them as the measurement covariance, ahead of sigma_col and sigma. A supplied covariance is final: fill_scale is not applied to it. Kinds without a noise model ignore it. split_speed: a track is cut between two rows whose implied speed (m/s) is above this (a jump / ID switch). This and gap_max_speed are segmentation rules in m/s; the speeds of the output come from tssa.speed.SpeedCalculator. fill_gaps: fill the frames missing inside a track (False cuts the track at every gap instead). fill_max_gap: longest gap in frames that may be filled. gap_max_speed: fastest implied speed in m/s across a filled gap.

def with_overrides(self, **overrides) -> "SmoothConfig":
    """Copy with some settings replaced; an unknown name raises ValueError."""
    known = {f.name for f in fields(self)}
    bad = sorted(set(overrides) - known)
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown setting(s) {bad}; known: {sorted(known)}")
    return replace(self, **overrides)

for one segment, times t (n,), raw positions pos (n, 2 metres; filled rows hold interpolated

def register_method(name: str, defaults: dict, min_len: Callable[[dict], int], usable=None):
    """Decorator: register `fn(t, pos, ctx, **params) -> pos` as smoothing kind `name`."""

    def wrap(fn):
        REGISTRY[name] = Method(fn, dict(defaults), min_len, usable or (lambda ctx: len(ctx.interp)))
        return fn

    return wrap

    """Name a kind with fixed parameters, e.g. `sg7` = `sg` with win 7."""

def resolve(name: str, params: dict | None = None) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """Kind and merged parameters (kind defaults, preset, then `params`) of a method name; ValueError if unknown."""
    if name in PRESETS:
        kind, preset = PRESETS[name]
    elif name in REGISTRY:
        kind, preset = name, {}
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown method {name!r}; available: {sorted(set(PRESETS) | set(REGISTRY))}")
    merged = {**REGISTRY[kind].defaults, **preset}
    bad = sorted(set(params or {}) - set(merged))
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown parameter(s) {bad} for method {name!r}; known: {sorted(merged)}")
    merged.update(params or {})
    return kind, merged

@register_method("sg", {"win": 7, "order": 2, "med": 3}, min_len=lambda p: int(p["win"]))
def median_sg(t: np.ndarray, pos: np.ndarray, ctx: SegmentContext, win: int, order: int, med: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Median filter (`med` = 1 skips it) then Savitzky-Golay (mode='interp'); the smoothed position."""
    _check_odd(win, order)
    if med < 1 or med % 2 == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"med must be an odd integer >= 1, got {med}")
    m = ndimage.median_filter(pos, size=(med, 1), mode="nearest") if med > 1 else pos
    return savgol_filter(m, win, order, axis=0, mode="interp")

docs.title: rts_smooth
docs.text:
rts_smooth(
    pos: ndarray, R: ndarray, dt: float, q: float
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Constant-velocity Kalman filter + RTS smoother; rows with NaN pos get no measurement update.

The forward pass starts at the first measured row i0, from the state of the first two measured rows. Rows before i0 take the smoothed state at i0 extrapolated backward at its constant velocity. Raises ValueError with fewer than 2 measured rows.

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/methods.py 
def rts_smooth(pos: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, dt: float, q: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Constant-velocity Kalman filter + RTS smoother; rows with NaN pos get no measurement update.

    The forward pass starts at the first measured row `i0`, from the state of the first two measured rows. Rows
    before `i0` take the smoothed state at `i0` extrapolated backward at its constant velocity. Raises ValueError
    with fewer than 2 measured rows.
    """
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    n = len(pos)
    meas = np.flatnonzero(~np.isnan(pos[:, 0]))
    if len(meas) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"rts_smooth needs at least 2 measured rows, got {len(meas)}")
    I2 = np.eye(2)
    F = np.block([[I2, dt * I2], [np.zeros((2, 2)), I2]])
    Q = q * np.block([[dt**3 / 3 * I2, dt**2 / 2 * I2], [dt**2 / 2 * I2, dt * I2]])
    H = np.hstack([I2, np.zeros((2, 2))])
    i0, i1 = meas[0], meas[1]
    x0 = np.concatenate([pos[i0], (pos[i1] - pos[i0]) / ((i1 - i0) * dt)])
    xp, Pp = np.zeros((n, 4)), np.zeros((n, 4, 4))
    xf, Pf = np.zeros((n, 4)), np.zeros((n, 4, 4))
    x, P = x0, np.diag(RTS_P0)
    for k in range(i0, n):
        if k > i0:
            x, P = F @ x, F @ P @ F.T + Q
        xp[k], Pp[k] = x, P
        if not np.isnan(pos[k, 0]):
            S = H @ P @ H.T + R[k]
            K = P @ H.T @ np.linalg.inv(S)
            x = x + K @ (pos[k] - H @ x)
            P = (np.eye(4) - K @ H) @ P
        xf[k], Pf[k] = x, P
    xs = xf.copy()
    for k in range(n - 2, i0 - 1, -1):
        C = Pf[k] @ F.T @ np.linalg.inv(Pp[k + 1])
        xs[k] = xf[k] + C @ (xs[k + 1] - xp[k + 1])
    if i0 > 0:  # unmeasured prefix: constant-velocity extrapolation back from the smoothed state at i0
        back = (i0 - np.arange(i0))[:, None] * dt
        xs[:i0, :2] = xs[i0, :2] - back * xs[i0, 2:]
        xs[:i0, 2:] = xs[i0, 2:]
    return xs[:, :2], xs[:, 2:]

rts(

    pos: ndarray,
    ctx: SegmentContext,
    q: float,
    sigma: float,
    fill_scale: float,
) -> np.ndarray

RTS smoother on the observed positions (the position part of the state).

Measured rows are interp < 2 (legacy) or ctx.meas (segmented mode). A row's covariance is its per-row covariance where one is given (final: never scaled); otherwise the std-dev sigma metres (the per-row sigma column replaces it where given), times fill_scale on rows filled upstream (interp = 1).

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/methods.py 
@register_method(
    "rts", {"q": 0.5, "sigma": 0.05, "fill_scale": FILL_MEAS_SCALE}, min_len=lambda p: 2,
    usable=lambda ctx: int(ctx.measured().sum()),
)  # fmt: skip
def rts(t: np.ndarray, pos: np.ndarray, ctx: SegmentContext, q: float, sigma: float, fill_scale: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """RTS smoother on the observed positions (the position part of the state).

    Measured rows are interp < 2 (legacy) or `ctx.meas` (segmented mode). A row's covariance is its per-row
    covariance where one is given (final: never scaled); otherwise the std-dev `sigma` metres (the per-row sigma
    column replaces it where given), times `fill_scale` on rows filled upstream (interp = 1).
    """
    if q <= 0 or sigma <= 0 or fill_scale <= 0:
        raise ValueError("q, sigma and fill_scale must be positive")
    ok = ctx.measured()
    s = np.where(np.isnan(ctx.sigma), sigma, ctx.sigma) * np.where(ctx.interp == 1, fill_scale, 1.0)
    R = np.zeros((len(t), 2, 2))
    R[ok] = (s[ok] ** 2)[:, None, None] * np.eye(2)
    if ctx.cov is not None:
        own = ok & np.isfinite(ctx.cov).all(axis=(1, 2))
        _check_cov(ctx.cov[own])
        R[own] = ctx.cov[own]
    obs = ctx.obs.copy()
    obs[~ok] = np.nan
    return rts_smooth(obs, R, ctx.dt, q)[0]

def smooth_segment(kind: str, params: dict, t: np.ndarray, pos: np.ndarray, ctx: SegmentContext) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]:
    """Apply a method to one segment; a segment shorter than the method's minimum gets the raw positions (fallback)."""
    spec = REGISTRY[kind]
    if spec.usable(ctx) < spec.min_len(params):
        return pos, True
    return spec.fn(t, pos, ctx, **params), False

docs.title: segments
docs.text:
Segmentation of ground tracks for smoothing: duplicates, jumps, gap reasons, fill grid.

Inputs

track tables with frame, track, the two position columns (metres), optionally interp (0 detected, 1 filled upstream) and a per-row sigma; an optional reference table (the tracks before gaps were emptied or filled upstream) that tells jump gaps from plain gaps.

Outputs: prepare -> table with canonical columns _x, _y (metres), _sigma, interp, deduplicated and sorted jump_split -> boolean split flags between consecutive rows of one track (implied speed rule) jump_gaps -> (track, first, last) of the gaps between detected rows that jump classify_gaps -> table (track, gap_id, first, last, length, implied_speed, reason, fill) build_grid -> grid: one row per frame of every segment, filled gaps included, in LOCAL metres (grid.attrs["origin"] = (X0, Y0) is the origin of the local frame) structure -> the structural table only (track, frame, seg, seg_len, interp, fill_reason, gap_id), with rows of missing positions kept (allow_missing); no positions, so none can be reused

docs.text:
prepare(
    df: DataFrame,
    cfg: SmoothConfig,
    allow_missing: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame

Copy with canonical _x, _y, _sigma, covariance and interp columns, sorted by track and frame, repeated rows dropped.

Raises ValueError for a missing required column, or for a non-finite position unless allow_missing.

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/segments.py 
def prepare(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: SmoothConfig, allow_missing: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Copy with canonical `_x`, `_y`, `_sigma`, covariance and `interp` columns, sorted by track and frame, repeated
    rows dropped.

    Raises ValueError for a missing required column, or for a non-finite position unless `allow_missing`.
    """
    xc, yc = cfg.xy_cols
    need = ["frame", "track", xc, yc] + ([cfg.sigma_col] if cfg.sigma_col else []) + list(cfg.cov_cols or [])
    missing = [c for c in need if c not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"tracks lack required column(s) {missing}")
    out = df.copy()
    out["_x"], out["_y"] = out[xc].astype(float), out[yc].astype(float)
    out["_sigma"] = out[cfg.sigma_col].astype(float) if cfg.sigma_col else np.nan
    for canon, col in zip(COV, cfg.cov_cols or (None, None, None)):
        out[canon] = out[col].astype(float) if col else np.nan
    if "interp" not in out.columns:
        out["interp"] = 0
    if not allow_missing and not np.isfinite(out[["_x", "_y"]].to_numpy()).all():
        raise ValueError(f"position columns {cfg.xy_cols} contain NaN or infinite values")
    out = out[~out.duplicated(["frame", "track"], keep="first")]
    return out.sort_values(["track", "frame"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    f: ndarray, xy: ndarray, *, speed: float, fps: float

Flag the pairs of consecutive rows (length n - 1) whose implied speed (m/s) is above speed.

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/segments.py 
def jump_split(f: np.ndarray, xy: np.ndarray, *, speed: float, fps: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Flag the pairs of consecutive rows (length n - 1) whose implied speed (m/s) is above `speed`."""
    step = np.hypot(np.diff(xy[:, 0]), np.diff(xy[:, 1]))
    return step / (np.maximum(np.diff(f), 1) / fps) > speed

def jump_gaps(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: SmoothConfig) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """Return `(track, first frame, last frame)` of the gaps between detected rows (interp 0) that jump."""
    gaps = []
    for tid, obs in df[df["interp"] == 0].sort_values("frame").groupby("track"):
        if len(obs) < 2:
            continue
        f = obs["frame"].to_numpy()
        flag = jump_split(f, obs[["_x", "_y"]].to_numpy(dtype=float), speed=cfg.split_speed, fps=cfg.fps)
        gaps += [(int(tid), int(f[k]), int(f[k + 1])) for k in np.flatnonzero(flag & (np.diff(f) > 1))]
    return gaps

Classify every frame gap of a prepared table; first match wins.

ref_jumps are the jump gaps of the reference table (see jump_gaps). A plain gap is overlap when the reference was given (verified) and unverified otherwise; both are filled when cfg.fill_gaps is on.

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/segments.py 
def classify_gaps(df: pd.DataFrame, ref_jumps: list[tuple[int, int, int]], cfg: SmoothConfig, *, verified: bool) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Classify every frame gap of a prepared table; first match wins.

    `ref_jumps` are the jump gaps of the reference table (see `jump_gaps`). A plain gap is `overlap` when the
    reference was given (`verified`) and `unverified` otherwise; both are filled when `cfg.fill_gaps` is on.
    """
    pr = _pairs(df, cfg)
    pr = pr[pr["same"] & (pr["last"] - pr["first"] > 1)].reset_index(drop=True)
    x, y = df["_x"].to_numpy(), df["_y"].to_numpy()
    i = pr["i"].to_numpy()
    span = (pr["last"] - pr["first"]).to_numpy()
    length = span - 1
    speed = np.hypot(x[i + 1] - x[i], y[i + 1] - y[i]) / (span / cfg.fps)
    jumped = pr["jump"].to_numpy()
    jump_by_track = {}
    if ref_jumps:
        jt = pd.DataFrame(ref_jumps, columns=["track", "first", "last"])
        jump_by_track = {t: g[["first", "last"]].to_numpy() for t, g in jt.groupby("track")}
    plain = OVERLAP if verified else UNVERIFIED
    out = []
    for k, (t, first, last) in enumerate(zip(pr["track"], pr["first"], pr["last"])):
        rows = jump_by_track.get(t)
        if jumped[k]:
            reason = JUMP
        elif rows is not None and ((rows[:, 0] <= first) & (last <= rows[:, 1])).any():
            reason = JUMP
        elif length[k] > cfg.fill_max_gap:
            reason = LONG
        elif speed[k] > cfg.gap_max_speed:
            reason = SPEED
        else:
            reason = plain
        out.append(reason)
    gaps = pd.DataFrame({
        "track": pr["track"].astype("int64"), "gap_id": np.arange(len(pr)), "first": pr["first"].astype("int64"),
        "last": pr["last"].astype("int64"), "length": length.astype("int64"), "implied_speed": speed,
        "reason": pd.Series(out, dtype=object),
    })  # fmt: skip
    gaps["fill"] = gaps["reason"].isin(FILL_REASONS) & cfg.fill_gaps
    return gaps[GAP_COLUMNS]

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/segments.py 
def build_grid(df: pd.DataFrame, gaps: pd.DataFrame, cfg: SmoothConfig) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-frame grid of all segments: split at jumps and unfilled gaps, interp = 2 rows inside filled gaps."""
    obs = df[["frame", "track", "interp", "_sigma", *COV, "_x", "_y"]].copy()
    origin = (float(np.floor(obs["_x"].min())), float(np.floor(obs["_y"].min())))
    obs["x_obs"], obs["y_obs"] = obs["_x"] - origin[0], obs["_y"] - origin[1]
    obs["x_raw"], obs["y_raw"] = obs["x_obs"], obs["y_obs"]
    obs["sigma"] = obs["_sigma"]
    obs["fill_reason"], obs["gap_id"] = "", -1
    pr = _pairs(df, cfg)
    pr = pr[pr["same"]].merge(
        gaps[["track", "first", "last", "gap_id", "reason", "fill"]], how="left", on=["track", "first", "last"]
    )
    gapped = (pr["last"] - pr["first"]) > 1
    fills = gapped & pr["fill"].eq(True) & ~pr["jump"]
    cut = pr["jump"] | (gapped & ~fills)
    boundary = np.ones(len(obs), bool)  # track starts stay True
    boundary[pr["i"].to_numpy() + 1] = cut.to_numpy()
    obs["seg"] = np.cumsum(boundary) - 1
    fp = pr[fills]
    if len(fp):
        lo = fp["i"].to_numpy()
        count = (fp["last"] - fp["first"] - 1).to_numpy()
        rep = np.repeat(np.arange(len(fp)), count)
        step = np.arange(count.sum()) - np.repeat(np.cumsum(count) - count, count) + 1
        t = step / (fp["last"] - fp["first"]).to_numpy()[rep]
        a = lo[rep]
        fill = pd.DataFrame({
            "frame": fp["first"].to_numpy()[rep] + step, "track": fp["track"].to_numpy()[rep],
            "seg": obs["seg"].to_numpy()[a],
        })  # fmt: skip
        for col in ("x_raw", "y_raw"):
            v = obs[col].to_numpy()
            fill[col] = v[a] + t * (v[a + 1] - v[a])
        fill["interp"] = 2
        fill["fill_reason"] = fp["reason"].to_numpy()[rep]
        fill["gap_id"] = fp["gap_id"].astype("int64").to_numpy()[rep]
        grid = pd.concat([obs, fill], ignore_index=True).sort_values(["track", "frame"], kind="stable")
    else:
        grid = obs
    grid["seg_len"] = grid.groupby("seg")["frame"].transform("size")
    grid = grid.reindex(columns=GRID_COLUMNS).reset_index(drop=True)
    grid.attrs["origin"] = origin
    return grid

docs.text:
structure(
    df: DataFrame, ref: DataFrame | None, cfg: SmoothConfig
) -> pd.DataFrame

Structural table of a prepared table that may hold rows without a finite position.

Jumps and gaps are classified on the finite rows only; a run of missing rows is part of the gap around it: - interior run in a filled gap: kept in that segment with its own interp, fill_reason = "no_position"; - interior run in a gap that is not filled (split), a prefix, a suffix, or a track with no finite row: seg = -1, fill_reason = "no_position", never extrapolated. Frames with no input row inside a filled gap are inserted as interp = 2, as build_grid does. Columns: STRUCT_COLUMNS; seg_len is 0 on seg = -1 rows.

Source code in src/tssa/smooth/segments.py 
def structure(df: pd.DataFrame, ref: pd.DataFrame | None, cfg: SmoothConfig) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Structural table of a prepared table that may hold rows without a finite position.

    Jumps and gaps are classified on the finite rows only; a run of missing rows is part of the gap around it:
    - interior run in a filled gap: kept in that segment with its own interp, fill_reason = "no_position";
    - interior run in a gap that is not filled (split), a prefix, a suffix, or a track with no finite row:
      seg = -1, fill_reason = "no_position", never extrapolated.
    Frames with no input row inside a filled gap are inserted as interp = 2, as `build_grid` does.
    Columns: STRUCT_COLUMNS; seg_len is 0 on seg = -1 rows.
    """
    has = np.isfinite(df[["_x", "_y"]].to_numpy(dtype=float)).all(axis=1)
    fin = df[has].reset_index(drop=True)
    if fin.empty:
        struct = pd.DataFrame({c: pd.Series(dtype="int64") for c in ["track", "frame", "seg", "interp", "gap_id"]})
        struct["fill_reason"] = pd.Series(dtype=object)
    else:
        verified = ref is not None
        ref_jumps = jump_gaps(ref[np.isfinite(ref[["_x", "_y"]].to_numpy(dtype=float)).all(axis=1)], cfg) if verified else []
        gaps = classify_gaps(fin, ref_jumps, cfg, verified=verified)
        struct = build_grid(fin, gaps, cfg)[["track", "frame", "seg", "interp", "fill_reason", "gap_id"]].copy()
    miss = df.loc[~has, ["track", "frame", "interp"]]
    if len(miss):
        key = pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(struct[["track", "frame"]])
        mkey = pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(miss[["track", "frame"]])
        inside = key.isin(mkey)  # inserted (interp = 2) rows of a filled gap at frames that have a missing input row
        m_int = pd.Series(miss["interp"].to_numpy(), index=mkey)
        struct.loc[inside, "interp"] = m_int.reindex(key[inside]).to_numpy()
        struct.loc[inside, "fill_reason"] = NO_POSITION
        outside = miss[~mkey.isin(key)]
        extra = pd.DataFrame({"track": outside["track"].to_numpy(), "frame": outside["frame"].to_numpy(), "seg": -1,
                              "interp": outside["interp"].to_numpy(), "fill_reason": NO_POSITION, "gap_id": -1})
        struct = pd.concat([struct, extra], ignore_index=True)
    struct = struct.sort_values(["track", "frame"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
    seg = struct["seg"].to_numpy()
    sizes = struct[seg >= 0].groupby("seg")["frame"].transform("size")
    struct["seg_len"] = 0
    struct.loc[seg >= 0, "seg_len"] = sizes.to_numpy()
    for c in ("frame", "seg", "seg_len", "interp", "gap_id"):
        struct[c] = struct[c].astype("int64")
    return struct[STRUCT_COLUMNS]

docs.title: smoother
docs.text:
TrackSmoother: segment projected ground tracks, fill gaps, smooth the positions with a chosen method.

track tables with frame, track and two position columns in metres (a ground plane the user projected

beforehand; default names x, y), optionally interp (0 detected, 1 filled upstream), a per-row sigma column and three per-row covariance columns. Any other columns are carried through. No homography is involved.

Outputs: the input columns first, unchanged and in their order (NaN on rows filled here), then the added columns. smooth() adds seg, fill_reason, smooth (two columns) and fallback (1 = segment too short for the method, raw positions copied); interp (0 detected, 1 filled upstream, 2 filled here) is updated in place, or added at the front when the input lacks it. compare() adds seg, fill_reason, then (two columns) and fb_ per method . Speeds are not computed here: pass the smoothed positions to tssa.speed.SpeedCalculator.

Segmenting once, smoothing many times (design docs/2026-11-10-footprint-design.md, section 5.2): segment() returns the structural table only (track, frame, seg, seg_len, interp, fill_reason, gap_id). smooth(..., segmented=True) takes those columns from its input and does not re-segment: a row is a measurement exactly when seg >= 0 and its position is finite (interp is provenance only), observations come only from this call's positions, and seg = -1 rows come back with NaN positions.

def segment(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame, ref_tracks: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
            allow_missing: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:  # fmt: skip
    """Structural table (track, frame, seg, seg_len, interp, fill_reason, gap_id): split at jumps, fill gaps.

    One row per input row (repeated (track, frame) rows dropped) plus the inserted rows (interp = 2). No
    positions are returned. With `allow_missing`, rows without a finite position are kept: an interior run inside
    a filled gap stays in that segment (fill_reason "no_position"); any other such row gets seg = -1.
    """
    df = segments.prepare(tracks, self.config, allow_missing=allow_missing)
    ref = segments.prepare(ref_tracks, self.config, allow_missing=True) if ref_tracks is not None else None
    return segments.structure(df, ref, self.config)

def smooth(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame, ref_tracks: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
           segmented: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:  # fmt: skip
    """Smoothed table for the configured method (see the module docstring for `segmented`)."""
