def compare(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame, methods=None, ref_tracks: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
            segmented: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:  # fmt: skip
    """Every method side by side on one segmentation and gap fill.

    `methods` is a list of names or a dict name -> parameters; None means every preset (ma, sg5, sg7, rts).
    """
    if methods is None:
        methods = list(PRESETS)
    specs = list(methods.items()) if isinstance(methods, dict) else [(m, None) for m in methods]
    resolved = [(name, *resolve(name, p)) for name, p in specs]
    if segmented:
        return self._smooth_segmented(tracks, resolved, ref_tracks, single=False)
    df, grid = self._grid(tracks, ref_tracks)
    out = self._apply(grid, resolved)
    return self._finish(out, grid, df, [n for n, _, _ in resolved], single=False)

def __init__(self, fps: float = 10.0, xy_cols: tuple = ("x", "y"), interval: int | None = None,
             units: str = "imperial") -> None:  # fmt: skip
    if fps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("fps must be positive")
    if len(xy_cols) != 2 or xy_cols[0] == xy_cols[1]:
        raise ValueError(f"xy_cols must be a pair of two different column names, got {xy_cols!r}")
    if interval is not None and (int(interval) != interval or interval < 2):
        raise ValueError(f"interval must be None or an integer >= 2, got {interval!r}")
    if units not in UNITS:
        raise ValueError(f"units must be one of {UNITS}, got {units!r}")
    self.fps, self.xy_cols, self.interval, self.units = fps, tuple(xy_cols), interval, units

def calculate(self, tracks: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The input table plus vx, vy and speed; rows with a missing position get NaN."""
    xc, yc = self.xy_cols
    missing = [c for c in ("frame", "track", xc, yc) if c not in tracks.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"tracks lack required column(s) {missing}")
    clash = sorted(set(ADDED) & set(tracks.columns))
    if clash:
        raise ValueError(f"input columns {clash} clash with columns the calculator adds; rename them first")
    keys = ["track", "seg"] if "seg" in tracks.columns else ["track"]
    frames = tracks["frame"].to_numpy()
    pos = tracks[[xc, yc]].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    vel = np.full((len(tracks), 2), np.nan)
    for rows in tracks.groupby(keys, sort=False).indices.values():
        rows = rows[np.argsort(frames[rows], kind="stable")]
        rows = rows[np.isfinite(pos[rows]).all(axis=1)]
        f = frames[rows]
        if len(rows) < 2:
            continue
        if (np.diff(f) == 0).any():
            raise ValueError(f"track {tracks['track'].to_numpy()[rows[0]]} has repeated frames within a segment")
        t = f / self.fps
        vel[rows] = frame_velocity(t, pos[rows]) if self.interval is None else block_velocity(f, t, pos[rows], self.interval)
    vel = vel * SPEED_PER_MPS[self.units]
    out = tracks.copy()
    out["vx"], out["vy"] = vel[:, 0].round(3), vel[:, 1].round(3)
    out["speed"] = np.hypot(vel[:, 0], vel[:, 1]).round(3)
    out.attrs["speed_unit"] = SPEED_UNIT[self.units]
    return out

def frame_velocity(t: np.ndarray, pos: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """(n, 2) velocity at every sample: central differences (one-sided at the ends); NaN for a single sample."""
    if len(t) < 2:
        return np.full((len(t), 2), np.nan)
    return np.gradient(pos, t, axis=0)

docs.title: block_velocity
docs.text:
block_velocity(
    frames: ndarray, t: ndarray, pos: ndarray, interval: int
) -> np.ndarray

(n, 2) block velocity: blocks start every interval frames from the first frame.

The velocity of a block is the displacement from the position at its first frame to the position at the start of the next block, over the elapsed time; every row of the block carries it. The last block ends at the last row (it may be shorter and uses its own duration) and takes all the rows from its start on. A row missing at a block boundary is replaced by the next row. NaN where a block holds a single row.

Source code in src/tssa/speed/calculator.py 
def block_velocity(frames: np.ndarray, t: np.ndarray, pos: np.ndarray, interval: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """(n, 2) block velocity: blocks start every `interval` frames from the first frame.

    The velocity of a block is the displacement from the position at its first frame to the position at the start
    of the next block, over the elapsed time; every row of the block carries it. The last block ends at the last
    row (it may be shorter and uses its own duration) and takes all the rows from its start on. A row missing at a
    block boundary is replaced by the next row. NaN where a block holds a single row.
    """
    first, last = int(frames[0]), int(frames[-1])
    starts = np.arange(first, last, interval)
    out = np.full((len(frames), 2), np.nan)
    if not len(starts):
        return out
    lo = np.searchsorted(frames, starts, side="left")
    hi = np.minimum(np.searchsorted(frames, starts + interval, side="left"), len(frames) - 1)
    ok = hi > lo
    vel = np.full((len(starts), 2), np.nan)
    vel[ok] = (pos[hi[ok]] - pos[lo[ok]]) / (t[hi[ok]] - t[lo[ok]])[:, None]
    return vel[np.searchsorted(starts, frames, side="right") - 1]

Approximate pinhole camera fitted to a ground homography, and the hub -> contact drop.

Ported from the speed study's camera.py (snapshot docs/study-snapshot-2026-11-10.json; design docs/2026-11-10-footprint-design.md section 8). Changes from the study: no OpenCV (scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation replaces cv2.Rodrigues, a normalised DLT replaces the initial cv2.findHomography(..., 0)); the settings are arguments; the ground model is a GroundModel (image size and pixel spaces from it).

World frame: right-handed (E, N, Up), metres. Public functions take and return world coordinates (e.g. UTM); the camera keeps R and C relative to its own calibration origin (PinholeCamera.origin). The camera works on UNDISTORTED pixels; the ground model's distort is applied afterwards.

def project(self, XYZ) -> np.ndarray:
    """World (n, 3) -> undistorted pixels (n, 2); NaN for points not in front of the camera."""
    X = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(XYZ, dtype=float)) - self._origin3
    uv, depth = _project_local(self.f, self.R, self.C, self.cx, self.cy, X)
    uv[depth <= 0] = np.nan
    return uv

def ray(self, uv_undist):
    """Undistorted pixels (n, 2) -> (camera centre world (3,), unit world directions (n, 3))."""
    uv = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(uv_undist, dtype=float))
    d_cam = np.column_stack([(uv[:, 0] - self.cx) / self.f, (uv[:, 1] - self.cy) / self.f, np.ones(len(uv))])
    d = d_cam @ self.R  # R.T @ d_cam, row-wise
    return self.C + self._origin3, d / np.linalg.norm(d, axis=1, keepdims=True)

fit(
    ground,
    zone,
    f_fixed: float | None = None,
    free_principal: bool = True,
    pp_prior: float = 0.001,
) -> "PinholeCamera"

Least-squares pinhole fit to the ground model over a 1 m grid in the zone (world coordinates).

Correspondences are world (x, y, 0) -> ground.world_to_undistorted pixels. Fitted: f (unless f_fixed), (cx, cy) when free_principal (starting at the image centre, else fixed there), R and C. With a free principal point a single ground plane fixes (f, cx, cy) only up to a one-parameter family of exact fits; two weak prior residuals pp_prior * (cx - cx0, cy - cy0) pick the member nearest the image centre (study ruling R18). If the least squares does not converge, the camera is returned with converged=False and a RuntimeWarning.

Source code in src/tssa/transform/camera.py 
@classmethod
def fit(cls, ground, zone, f_fixed: float | None = None, free_principal: bool = True,
        pp_prior: float = 1e-3) -> "PinholeCamera":  # fmt: skip
    """Least-squares pinhole fit to the ground model over a 1 m grid in the zone (world coordinates).

    Correspondences are world (x, y, 0) -> `ground.world_to_undistorted` pixels. Fitted: f (unless f_fixed),
    (cx, cy) when free_principal (starting at the image centre, else fixed there), R and C. With a free principal
    point a single ground plane fixes (f, cx, cy) only up to a one-parameter family of exact fits; two weak prior
    residuals `pp_prior * (cx - cx0, cy - cy0)` pick the member nearest the image centre (study ruling R18).
    If the least squares does not converge, the camera is returned with `converged=False` and a RuntimeWarning.
    """
    g = GroundModel.wrap(ground)
    EN = zone_grid(zone)
    uv_u = np.asarray(g.world_to_undistorted(EN), dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(uv_u).all(axis=1)
    EN, uv_u = EN[ok], uv_u[ok]
    free = bool(free_principal)
    n_par = 6 + (f_fixed is None) + 2 * free
    need = max(4, -(-(n_par - 2 * free) // 2))  # the prior adds 2 residuals when free
    if len(EN) < need:
        raise ValueError(f"PinholeCamera.fit: only {len(EN)} finite correspondences in the zone, need {need}")
    c = zone.centroid
    origin = np.floor([c.x, c.y])
    X = np.column_stack([EN - origin, np.zeros(len(EN))])
    cx0, cy0 = g.image_size[0] / 2.0, g.image_size[1] / 2.0

    Hw2i = _dlt(X[:, :2], uv_u)
    f0, R0, C0 = _decompose(Hw2i, cx0, cy0, f_fixed)
    rvec0 = _rotvec(R0)

    def unpack(p):  # p = [f?] + [cx, cy]? + rvec + C
        i = 0
        if f_fixed is None:
            f, i = p[0], 1
        else:
            f = float(f_fixed)
        if free:
            cx, cy, i = p[i], p[i + 1], i + 2
        else:
            cx, cy = cx0, cy0
        return f, cx, cy, Rotation.from_rotvec(p[i:i + 3]).as_matrix(), p[i + 3:i + 6]

    def resid(p):
        f, cx, cy, R, C = unpack(p)
        uv, _ = _project_local(f, R, C, cx, cy, X)
        r = (uv - uv_u).ravel()
        if free:
            r = np.concatenate([r, [pp_prior * (cx - cx0), pp_prior * (cy - cy0)]])
        return r

    p0 = np.concatenate([[f0] if f_fixed is None else [], [cx0, cy0] if free else [], rvec0, C0])
    sol = least_squares(resid, p0, method="lm", x_scale="jac", xtol=1e-15, ftol=1e-15, gtol=1e-15, max_nfev=2000)
    f, cx, cy, R, C = unpack(sol.x)
    if not sol.success:
        warnings.warn(f"PinholeCamera.fit: least squares did not converge (status {sol.status}: {sol.message}); "
                      "camera flagged converged=False", RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)  # fmt: skip
    return cls(f, R, C, cx, cy, origin, converged=bool(sol.success))

def look_at(C, target=(0, 0, 0), f=500.0, cx=320.0, cy=240.0, origin=(0, 0)) -> PinholeCamera:
    """Camera at C (world, 3) aimed at target (world, 3), with no roll (camera x-axis horizontal)."""
    C = np.asarray(C, dtype=float)
    fwd = np.asarray(target, dtype=float) - C
    fwd /= np.linalg.norm(fwd)
    right = np.cross(fwd, [0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    if np.linalg.norm(right) < 1e-9:
        raise ValueError("look_at: viewing direction is vertical, roll is undefined")
    right /= np.linalg.norm(right)
    down = np.cross(fwd, right)
    origin = np.asarray(origin, dtype=float)
    return PinholeCamera(f, np.vstack([right, down, fwd]), C - [origin[0], origin[1], 0.0], cx, cy, origin)

def zone_grid(zone, step: float = GRID_STEP_M) -> np.ndarray:
    """World (n, 2) points of a `step` m grid inside the zone."""
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = zone.bounds
    xs = np.arange(np.floor(x0), x1 + step, step)
    ys = np.arange(np.floor(y0), y1 + step, step)
    gx, gy = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    pts = np.column_stack([gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()])
    pts = pts[shapely.contains_xy(zone, pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1])]
    if len(pts) < 8:
        raise ValueError(f"zone too small for a camera fit: {len(pts)} grid points")
    return pts

def consistency(cam: PinholeCamera, ground, zone, rms_px: float = 1.0, max_px: float = 3.0) -> dict:
    """Camera z = 0 projection + distort vs world_to_image over the zone grid (px).

    ok needs rms <= rms_px, max <= max_px and a converged fit.
    """
    g = GroundModel.wrap(ground)
    EN = zone_grid(zone)
    uv_cam = np.asarray(g.distort(cam.project(np.column_stack([EN, np.zeros(len(EN))]))), dtype=float)
    uv_g = np.asarray(g.world_to_image(EN), dtype=float)
    err = np.linalg.norm(uv_cam - uv_g, axis=1)
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(err**2)))
    mx = float(np.max(err))
    return dict(rms_px=rms, max_px=mx, ok=bool(cam.converged and rms <= rms_px and mx <= max_px))

def sensitivity(ground, zone, base: PinholeCamera, scales=FOCAL_SCALES, free_principal: bool = True,
                pp_prior: float = 1e-3, rms_px: float = 1.0, max_px: float = 3.0) -> list[dict]:  # fmt: skip
    """Refit (cx, cy), R, C with f fixed at base.f x each scale; each refit reports its own ground residual."""
    out = []
    for s in scales:
        cam = PinholeCamera.fit(ground, zone, f_fixed=base.f * s, free_principal=free_principal, pp_prior=pp_prior)
        res = consistency(cam, ground, zone, rms_px, max_px)
        out.append(dict(scale=s, camera=cam, rms_px=res["rms_px"], max_px=res["max_px"], ok=res["ok"]))
    return out

Hub pixel (undistorted) -> ground contact world (n, 2): the ray meets z = r, then drops vertically.

Source code in src/tssa/transform/camera.py 
def hub_to_contact(cam: PinholeCamera, uv_undist, r_m) -> np.ndarray:
    """Hub pixel (undistorted) -> ground contact world (n, 2): the ray meets z = r, then drops vertically."""
    C, d = cam.ray(uv_undist)
    r = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(r_m, dtype=float), (len(d),))
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        t = (r - C[2]) / d[:, 2]
    hub = C + t[:, None] * d
    contact = hub[:, :2]
    contact[~(t > 0)] = np.nan
    return contact

A homography plus its distortion model and image size.

Build it with GroundModel.wrap(homography, image_size=None). The image size comes from the explicit argument, else from the homography's image_size attribute; the two must agree, and one of them must exist.

Source code in src/tssa/transform/ground.py 
def __init__(self, homography, image_size) -> None:
    for name in ("image_to_world", "world_to_image"):
        if not callable(getattr(homography, name, None)):
            raise ValueError(f"homography lacks {name}()")
    has_u = callable(getattr(homography, "undistort", None))
    has_d = callable(getattr(homography, "distort", None))
    if has_u != has_d:
        raise ValueError("homography has only one of undistort() / distort(); give both or neither")
    size = tuple(float(v) for v in image_size)
    if len(size) != 2 or not all(np.isfinite(size)) or min(size) <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"image_size must be a positive (width, height), got {image_size!r}")
    self.homography = homography
    self.image_size = size
    self.has_distortion = has_u

@classmethod
def wrap(cls, homography, image_size=None) -> "GroundModel":
    """Wrap `homography` (or re-check an existing GroundModel against `image_size`)."""
    if isinstance(homography, GroundModel):
        if image_size is not None and not np.allclose(image_size, homography.image_size):
            raise ValueError(f"image_size {tuple(image_size)} conflicts with the model's {homography.image_size}")
        return homography
    own = getattr(homography, "image_size", None)
    if image_size is not None and own is not None and not np.allclose(image_size, own):
        raise ValueError(f"image_size {tuple(image_size)} conflicts with the homography's image_size {tuple(own)}")
    size = image_size if image_size is not None else own
    if size is None:
        raise ValueError("image size unknown: pass image_size=(width, height); this homography does not carry one")
    return cls(homography, size)

def world_to_undistorted(self, world_xy) -> np.ndarray:
    """World metres -> undistorted pixels.

    For `DistortedHomography` this goes straight through its inner (undistorted image -> world) homography, so it
    avoids the iteration error of `distort()`; otherwise it is `undistort(world_to_image(.))`.
    """
    h = self.homography
    if isinstance(h, DistortedHomography):
        pts, squeeze = _points(world_xy, "world_xy")
        out = h.homography.world_to_image(pts - h.origin)
        return out[0] if squeeze else out
    return self.undistort(self.world_to_image(world_xy))

docs.title: homography
docs.text:
Homography utilities for image/world coordinate conversion.

This module provides HomographyTransform for mapping 2D image coordinates to 2D ground-plane world coordinates (and back) using a 3x3 projective transform.

Example

import numpy as np from tssa.transform.homography import HomographyTransform image_pts = np.array([[100, 200], [200, 200], [200, 300], [100, 300]]) world_pts = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0], [0.0, 1.0]]) h = HomographyTransform(image_pts, world_pts) h.image_to_world(np.array([150, 250])).shape (2,) h.world_to_image(np.array([[0.5, 0.5]])).shape (1, 2)

Practical workflow for roadside-camera use cases
  1. Collect ground control points (GCPs) in Google Earth Pro.
  2. Label corresponding pixel points on a reference video frame.
  3. Convert WGS84 latitude/longitude to metric coordinates (UTM or State Plane).
  4. Estimate homography with OpenCV from pixel points to ground-plane points.
Notes
  • This gives a ground-plane coordinate system, not full 3D calibration.
  • Use stable pavement/corner features and avoid elevated/moving objects.
  • Prefer 8+ distributed GCPs for robust estimation (minimum is 4).
  • Distortion, slope, and map/video time mismatch can introduce error.
  • OpenCV is needed only to fit a homography from point pairs. Loading a saved model (load_json, load_matrix) and projecting with it use NumPy only.

def __init__(
    self,
    image_points: np.ndarray,
    world_points: np.ndarray,
    method: int | None = None,
    ransac_reproj_threshold: float = 3.0,
) -> None:
    """Compute homography and inverse-homography matrices.

    Args:
        image_points: Image-space correspondences shaped ``(N, 2)`` with ``N >= 4``.
        world_points: World-space correspondences shaped ``(N, 2)`` with ``N >= 4``.
        method: OpenCV homography estimation method (e.g., ``cv2.RANSAC``, ``0`` for plain
            least squares). ``None`` (default) means ``cv2.RANSAC``.
        ransac_reproj_threshold: Reprojection threshold used when ``method`` is RANSAC-like.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If point arrays are invalid, mismatched in length, or homography fails.
        ValueError: If the estimated homography is singular and cannot be inverted.
    """
    self._ransac_threshold = ransac_reproj_threshold
    src = self._validate_points(image_points, min_points=4, name="image_points")
    dst = self._validate_points(world_points, min_points=4, name="world_points")

    if src.shape[0] != dst.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("image_points and world_points must contain the same number of points.")

    method = _CV_RANSAC if method is None else method
    H, mask = _cv2().findHomography(src, dst, method=method, ransacReprojThreshold=ransac_reproj_threshold)
    if H is None:
        raise ValueError("Failed to compute homography matrix from input points.")

    self.H = H.astype(np.float64)
    self.inlier_mask = mask
    self.n_points = int(src.shape[0])

    try:
        self.H_inv = np.linalg.inv(self.H)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError as exc:
        raise ValueError("Homography matrix is singular and cannot be inverted.") from exc

@classmethod
def load_matrix(cls, file_path: str) -> "HomographyTransform":
    """Load homography matrices from a NumPy ``.npz`` file.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a saved homography ``.npz`` file.

    Returns:
        A `HomographyTransform` instance populated from saved matrices.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If loaded ``H`` or ``H_inv`` does not have shape ``(3, 3)``.
    """
    data = np.load(file_path, allow_pickle=False)
    H = data["H"]
    H_inv = data["H_inv"]
    inlier_mask = data["inlier_mask"] if "inlier_mask" in data.files else None

    if H.shape != (3, 3) or H_inv.shape != (3, 3):
        raise ValueError("Saved matrices must both have shape (3, 3).")

    obj = cls.__new__(cls)
    obj.H = H.astype(np.float64)
    obj.H_inv = H_inv.astype(np.float64)
    obj.inlier_mask = inlier_mask
    obj.n_points = int(inlier_mask.size) if inlier_mask is not None else 0
    obj._ransac_threshold = 3.0
    return obj

@classmethod
def load_json(cls, file_path: str) -> "HomographyTransform":
    """Load a homography from a JSON file written by `save_json`.

    The model is restored directly from the saved values; no refitting is done.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a JSON file written by `save_json`.

    Returns:
        A `HomographyTransform` instance with the saved parameters.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the saved homography matrices do not have shape ``(3, 3)``.
    """
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    H = np.asarray(data["H"], dtype=np.float64)
    H_inv = np.asarray(data["H_inv"], dtype=np.float64)
    if H.shape != (3, 3) or H_inv.shape != (3, 3):
        raise ValueError("Saved matrices must both have shape (3, 3).")

    obj = cls.__new__(cls)
    obj.H = H
    obj.H_inv = H_inv
    mask = data.get("inlier_mask")
    obj.inlier_mask = None if mask is None else np.asarray(mask, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(-1, 1)
    obj.n_points = int(data["n_points"])
    obj._ransac_threshold = 3.0
    return obj

def reprojection_error(self, image_points: np.ndarray, world_points: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Compute mean reprojection error for validation.

    Projects world_points to image space and compares to the original image_points.
    Lower values indicate better fit.

    Args:
        image_points: Original image points shaped (N, 2).
        world_points: Original world points shaped (N, 2).

    Returns:
        Mean Euclidean distance between projected and original image points.
    """
    src = self._validate_points(image_points, min_points=1, name="image_points")
    dst = self._validate_points(world_points, min_points=1, name="world_points")

    if src.shape[0] != dst.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("image_points and world_points must contain the same number of points.")

    projected = self._project(dst, self.H_inv)
    errors = np.linalg.norm(src - projected, axis=1)
    return float(errors.mean())

DistortedHomography(
    image_points: ndarray,
    world_points: ndarray,
    image_size: tuple[int, int],
    n_coeffs: int = 2,
)

Radial lens distortion followed by a ground-plane homography.

Image points are corrected with p' = c + (p - c)(1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + ...), where r is the distance to the image centre c normalised by half the larger image side, and then mapped to world coordinates with a HomographyTransform. The distortion coefficients are optimised; the homography is re-fitted by least squares for each candidate. World coordinates are re-centred on their mean during fitting to keep large values (e.g., UTM) well conditioned.

Example

h = DistortedHomography(image_pts, world_pts, image_size=(640, 480)) h.image_to_world(np.array([320, 240])).shape (2,)

        image_size: Image ``(width, height)`` in pixels; sets the distortion centre.
        n_coeffs: Number of radial coefficients (``k1``, ``k2``, ...). Keep the total
            parameter count (``8 + n_coeffs``) well below ``2 * N``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If point arrays are invalid or there are too few points.
    """
    from scipy.optimize import least_squares

    min_points = max(4, (8 + n_coeffs + 1) // 2)
    src = HomographyTransform._validate_points(image_points, min_points=min_points, name="image_points")
    dst = HomographyTransform._validate_points(world_points, min_points=min_points, name="world_points")
    if src.shape[0] != dst.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("image_points and world_points must contain the same number of points.")

    width, height = image_size
    self.image_size = (float(width), float(height))
    self.center = np.array([width / 2.0, height / 2.0])
    self.scale = max(width, height) / 2.0
    self.origin = dst.mean(axis=0)
    local = dst - self.origin

    def residuals(k: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        undistorted = self._undistort(src, k)
        h = HomographyTransform(undistorted, local, method=0)
        return (h.image_to_world(undistorted) - local).ravel()

    self.k = least_squares(residuals, np.zeros(n_coeffs)).x
    self.homography = HomographyTransform(self._undistort(src, self.k), local, method=0)
    self.n_points = int(src.shape[0])

def distort(self, undistorted_xy: np.ndarray, n_iter: int = 20) -> np.ndarray:
    """Invert `undistort` by solving ``r_d (1 + k1 r_d^2 + ...) = r_u`` with Newton's method.

    Args:
        undistorted_xy: Corrected pixel point(s) ``(2,)`` or ``(N, 2)``.
        n_iter: Maximum number of Newton iterations.

    Returns:
        Raw image point(s), matching input rank.
    """
    points, squeeze_back = HomographyTransform._prepare_query_points(undistorted_xy, name="undistorted_xy")
    offset = (points - self.center) / self.scale
    r_u = np.linalg.norm(offset, axis=1)
    r_d = r_u.copy()
    for _ in range(n_iter):
        g = r_d * (1.0 + sum(kk * r_d ** (2 * (j + 1)) for j, kk in enumerate(self.k))) - r_u
        dg = 1.0 + sum((2 * j + 3) * kk * r_d ** (2 * (j + 1)) for j, kk in enumerate(self.k))
        step = g / dg
        r_d = r_d - step
        if np.all(np.abs(step) < 1e-12):
            break
    ratio = np.divide(r_d, r_u, out=np.ones_like(r_u), where=r_u > 0)
    out = self.center + offset * self.scale * ratio[:, None]
    return out[0] if squeeze_back else out

def world_to_image(self, world_xy: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Transform world point(s) ``(2,)`` or ``(N, 2)`` into raw image point(s)."""
    points, squeeze_back = HomographyTransform._prepare_query_points(world_xy, name="world_xy")

def rescale(self, new_size: tuple[int, int]) -> "DistortedHomography":
    """Return a copy of this model for images resized to ``new_size``.

    Distortion coefficients are unchanged (the radius is normalised); the centre, scale
    and homography are rescaled so the new model takes pixels from the resized image.

    Args:
        new_size: Target image ``(width, height)`` in pixels. Must have the same aspect
            ratio as the calibration image; crops and letterboxing are not supported.

    Returns:
        A new `DistortedHomography`; this instance is not modified.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``new_size`` is not positive or its aspect ratio differs.
    """
    new_w, new_h = float(new_size[0]), float(new_size[1])
    old_w, old_h = self.image_size
    if new_w <= 0 or new_h <= 0:
        raise ValueError("new_size must be positive.")
    s = new_w / old_w
    if not np.isclose(new_h / old_h, s, rtol=1e-3):
        raise ValueError(
            f"new_size {tuple(new_size)} must keep the aspect ratio of image_size {self.image_size}."
        )

    S = np.diag([s, s, 1.0])
    inner = HomographyTransform.__new__(HomographyTransform)
    inner.H = self.homography.H @ np.linalg.inv(S)
    inner.H_inv = S @ self.homography.H_inv
    inner.inlier_mask = None
    inner.n_points = self.homography.n_points
    inner._ransac_threshold = self.homography._ransac_threshold

    obj = type(self).__new__(type(self))
    obj.k = self.k.copy()
    obj.image_size = (new_w, new_h)
    obj.center = self.center * s
    obj.scale = self.scale * s
    obj.origin = self.origin.copy()
    obj.n_points = self.n_points
    obj.homography = inner
    return obj

@classmethod
def load_json(cls, file_path: str) -> "DistortedHomography":
    """Load a distorted homography from a JSON file written by `save_json`.

    The model is restored directly from the saved values; no refitting is done.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a JSON file written by `save_json`.

    Returns:
        A `DistortedHomography` instance with the saved parameters.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the saved homography matrices do not have shape ``(3, 3)``.
    """
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    H = np.asarray(data["H"], dtype=np.float64)
    H_inv = np.asarray(data["H_inv"], dtype=np.float64)
    if H.shape != (3, 3) or H_inv.shape != (3, 3):
        raise ValueError("Saved matrices must both have shape (3, 3).")

    inner = HomographyTransform.__new__(HomographyTransform)
    inner.H = H
    inner.H_inv = H_inv
    inner.inlier_mask = None
    inner.n_points = int(data["n_points"])
    inner._ransac_threshold = 3.0

    obj = cls.__new__(cls)
    obj.k = np.asarray(data["k"], dtype=np.float64)
    obj.center = np.asarray(data["center"], dtype=np.float64)
    obj.image_size = tuple(data.get("image_size", 2.0 * obj.center))
    obj.scale = float(data["scale"])
    obj.origin = np.asarray(data["origin"], dtype=np.float64)
    obj.n_points = int(data["n_points"])
    obj.homography = inner
    return obj

@classmethod
def load_matrix(cls, file_path: str) -> "DistortedHomography":
    """Load a distorted homography from a NumPy ``.npz`` file written by `save_matrix`.

    The model is restored directly from the saved arrays; no refitting is done.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a ``.npz`` file written by `save_matrix`.

    Returns:
        A `DistortedHomography` instance with the saved parameters.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the saved homography matrices do not have shape ``(3, 3)``.
    """
    data = np.load(file_path, allow_pickle=False)
    H = data["H"].astype(np.float64)
    H_inv = data["H_inv"].astype(np.float64)
    if H.shape != (3, 3) or H_inv.shape != (3, 3):
        raise ValueError("Saved matrices must both have shape (3, 3).")

    inner = HomographyTransform.__new__(HomographyTransform)
    inner.H = H
    inner.H_inv = H_inv
    inner.inlier_mask = None
    inner.n_points = int(data["n_points"])
    inner._ransac_threshold = 3.0

    obj = cls.__new__(cls)
    obj.k = data["k"].astype(np.float64)
    obj.center = data["center"].astype(np.float64)
    obj.image_size = tuple(data["image_size"]) if "image_size" in data else tuple(2.0 * obj.center)
    obj.scale = float(data["scale"])
    obj.origin = data["origin"].astype(np.float64)
    obj.n_points = int(data["n_points"])
    obj.homography = inner
    return obj

def kmz_to_csv(kmz_path: str, csv_path: str, verbose: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Convert KMZ point placemarks to a CSV file.

    Reads KML content from a KMZ archive, extracts only ``Placemark`` entries
    containing ``Point`` coordinates, and writes them to a CSV with columns:
    ``name``, ``lat``, ``lon``, ``alt``, and ``description``.

    Args:
        kmz_path: Input path to a ``.kmz`` file.
        csv_path: Output path for the generated ``.csv`` file.
        verbose: If ``True``, print progress messages.
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If ``kmz_path`` does not exist.
        RuntimeError: If no ``.kml`` file exists inside the KMZ archive.
        zipfile.BadZipFile: If the input is not a valid ZIP/KMZ archive.
        xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError: If KML XML parsing fails.
    """
    kmz_path = Path(kmz_path)
    csv_path = Path(csv_path)

    if not kmz_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(kmz_path)

    # 1) read doc.kml from kmz(zip)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(kmz_path, "r") as zf:
        # Prefer doc.kml, otherwise first *.kml
        kml_name = None
        names = zf.namelist()
        if "doc.kml" in names:
            kml_name = "doc.kml"
        else:
            for n in names:
                if n.lower().endswith(".kml"):
                    kml_name = n
                    break
        if not kml_name:
            raise RuntimeError("No .kml found inside the KMZ.")

        kml_bytes = zf.read(kml_name)

    # 2) parse KML
    root = ET.fromstring(kml_bytes)

    rows = []
    # Placemark can contain Point/LineString/Polygon; we extract Point coordinates only
    for pm in root.findall(".//kml:Placemark", KML_NS):
        name = pm.findtext("kml:name", default="", namespaces=KML_NS).strip()
        desc = pm.findtext("kml:description", default="", namespaces=KML_NS).strip()

        # Find Point coordinates
        coord_text = pm.findtext(".//kml:Point/kml:coordinates", default="", namespaces=KML_NS).strip()
        if not coord_text:
            continue

        # coordinates format: "lon,lat,alt" (alt optional), may have spaces/newlines
        # Some KML may have multiple coords; Point usually single coord
        coord_text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", coord_text).strip()
        first = coord_text.split(" ")[0]
        parts = first.split(",")

        lon = _to_float(parts[0]) if len(parts) >= 1 else None
        lat = _to_float(parts[1]) if len(parts) >= 2 else None
        alt = _to_float(parts[2]) if len(parts) >= 3 else 0.0  # default alt=0 if missing

        x, y = _to_utm(lat, lon)
        rows.append({
            "name": name,
            "lat": lat,
            "lon": lon,
            "alt": alt,
            "x": x,
            "y": y,
            "description": desc,
        })

    # 3) write CSV
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["name", "lat", "lon", "alt", "x", "y", "description"])
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    if verbose:
        print(f"Saved {len(rows)} point(s) to: {csv_path}")

    return df
